title: Verification Independence for Agentic AI: Designing Review Beyond Self-Correction and Multi-Agent Agreement

detail.title: Verification Independence for Agentic AI: Designing Review Beyond Self-Correction and Multi-Agent Agreement

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract:
As agentic artificial intelligence systems increasingly produce, evaluate, and act on their own outputs, review architectures face a structural problem: adding a second judgment does not necessarily create an independent basis for judgment. This paper proposes verification independence as a task-level design property for agentic AI. Verification independence asks whether the review process is sufficiently separated from the production process to surface errors that the producer is systematically unlikely to detect. The framework distinguishes four dimensions of independence: framing, evidence, mechanism, and authority. It also formalizes a four-function review architecture consisting of a producer, challenger, evidence checker, and acceptance owner.

The framework is positioned relative to research on LLM self-correction, chain-of-verification, multi-agent debate, LLM-as-a-judge, correlated model errors, and emerging agentic verification systems. Existing work shows both the value and limits of additional model-based review: structured verification can improve outputs, while multi-agent agreement, self-critique, and LLM judging remain vulnerable to shared assumptions, correlated errors, evaluator bias, and noisy rubric verification. The contribution here is integrative rather than a claim that any individual verification technique is new. It treats independence as a property of the relationship between production and review, not as a synonym for reviewer count or model diversity.

The central claim is that a reviewer can provide another judgment without providing another independent basis for judgment. For consequential agentic workflows, reliable verification therefore requires deliberate separation of review roles and, where feasible, external evidence, deterministic tests, independent tools, or distinct authority boundaries. The paper further introduces a qualitative independence checklist, risk-adjusted verification depth, and safeguards against erosion of independence in long-horizon workflows.

detail.abstract:
As artificial intelligence systems move from recommending actions to executing them, human oversight can no longer be treated as a binary choice between autonomy and a human-in-the-loop. This paper proposes an attention-constrained framework for designing agent autonomy around four variables: risk, reversibility, authority, and human attention. Risk, reversibility, and authority describe the consequence profile of an action; human attention describes the scarce oversight resource available to review it.

Drawing on research on levels of automation, appropriate reliance, automation bias, meaningful human oversight, and recent empirical studies of software agents, the paper argues that frequent approval requests can reduce rather than increase meaningful control when they consume attention faster than humans can exercise judgment.

The framework introduces an action-level oversight demand, an explicit human-attention budget, a lightweight extension for cumulative exposure across action sequences, and two design principles: exception-based oversight and approval quality over approval count. It further distinguishes four complementary modes of oversight—boundary setting, monitoring, escalation, and audit—and shows how they can be combined so that routine, bounded actions proceed without synchronous review while consequential or difficult-to-reverse actions receive concentrated human attention.

The paper also links these modes to task-level delegation contracts and proposes adaptive safeguards when review conditions appear to degrade. The contribution is integrative: reliable human oversight is framed not as maximizing human presence, but as allocating human judgment where its marginal value is highest.

detail.abstract: GenAI has transformed content from a medium consumed by humans into a resource consumed by machines. This paper proposes that content simultaneously carries two kinds of value: cultural value, realized through human reading and reception, and data value, realized through machine learning as training, alignment, evaluation, and retrieval material. The two values share a common origin in authenticity, originality, and systematicity, yet follow different scarcity logics. Tracing three historical revaluations of content-reproduction, attention, and corpora-the paper argues that the scarcity axis has shifted from human attention to trustworthy knowledge. Four propositions-value copresence, quality convergence, scarcity reversal, and value circulation-and a fivedimensional analytical framework are developed. The framework implies that content institutions hold their strongest position in alignment, evaluation, and retrieval, and that machine learning rights must be articulated within the bundle of rights to sustain the human-AI value cycle.

detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence can produce work that is functionally correct at delivery yet difficult to inspect, reconstruct, or modify later. This paper develops the concept of decision debt for AI-generated work: the future cost created when an acceptable output is retained without preserving the assumptions, evidence, dependencies, and interfaces needed to understand and safely change it.

The concept extends but does not replace technical debt. Whereas technical debt traditionally concerns implementation and architectural compromises that increase future maintenance cost, decision debt focuses on lost decision structure across software, analytical work, and agentic workflows.

The paper proposes four preservation properties—observability, traceability, modularity, and changeability—and a future-changeability test for evaluating whether AI-generated artifacts remain governable after delivery. It also offers a qualitative decision-debt checklist and a risk-adjusted preservation heuristic for deciding how much reconstruction evidence to retain. It also distinguishes external reconstruction evidence from private model reasoning: maintainability does not require access to an AI system's hidden chain of thought, but it does require sufficient records of sources, actions, tests, assumptions, and artifacts to reconstruct consequential decisions.

The contribution is integrative rather than a claim that provenance, maintainability, or technical debt are individually new. The central claim is that correctness is a present-tense property, while changeability is a future-tense property; reliable AI-generated work requires both.

title: Human Expert or Digital Information? Trust and Consumers' Reliance on Decision Aids for Financial Decisions

detail.title: Human Expert or Digital Information? Trust and Consumers' Reliance on Decision Aids for Financial Decisions

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationships with other people or organizations that could be perceived to have influenced this study.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency. The data used in this study, the Financial Planning Longitudinal Study, are made available to researchers by CFP Board, which underwrites the data collection.

detail.abstract: Consumers facing consequential financial decisions increasingly combine two kinds of decision aid: a human expert and digital information sources. Research on decision aids has examined how people weigh advice within a single decision, but not when acquiring a digital aid leads them to abandon a human one. We study this choice in a prospective two-wave panel of 3,354 mass affluent U.S. households, measuring antecedents in 2024 and decision-aid portfolios in 2025. Among the 1,327 households using a financial professional in 2024, prior reliance on digital information raises the probability of dropping the professional by 12.4 percentage points against an 18.0 percent base rate, while trust in the professional, financial complexity and wealth each reduce it. Trust conditions the effect of the digital aid: among households that trust their professional “a lot” prior digital use is not associated with dropping the professional (2.1 points, 95% CI −3.9 to 8.2), whereas among those that trust them “somewhat” it raises the probability by 17.5 points (95% CI 8.6 to 26.5). Financial literacy and fee sensitivity do not predict exit. A segmentation on these two indicators isolates 11 percent of advised clients who account for 24 percent of exits. The findings show that a digital aid substitutes for a human expert chiefly where reliance on the expert rests on weak trust, and they point to trust measurement as a practical input to retention analytics and to the design of hybrid advisory systems.

detail.abstract: This essay reports a negative result from a governed software build. Proteus is a deterministic, offline Windows and Python application designed to transform a cell phone photograph into a multimodal portfolio — a painting, a text artifact, and a piece of music — each governed jointly by the source photograph and by a pinned artistic referent. It was built between 14 August and 19 September 2026 by the author (a non-programmer) who directed two frontier large language models. Across thirty-six days and at least ten version series, one modality reached provisional artistic acceptance: music. Painting, poetry, and text did not. Reproducible execution was established and repeatedly verified, but the intended combination of structural image dependence, referent governance, and artistic acceptance was established in no modality, including the accepted one. A unit-test archive of fourteen Portfolio artifacts supports the central claims with measurements: all twenty-two rendered paintings carry conformance status, and five of six English sonnets, each naming a different pinned Shakespearean parent, share one fourteen-line skeleton at 73.1 to 85.0 per cent token-position identity. The essay argues that reproducible execution, source influence, referent influence, artistic acceptance, and accurate self-description are five distinct properties, and that success on one establishes none of the others. The proposed mechanism is a coupling between models that generate locally plausible implementations and a director able to judge artifacts but not to verify them.

detail.abstract: India's web development sector is among the largest in the world by the number of people working in it, and among the least documented. This paper sets out what can be established from primary and semi-primary sources, meaning industry association data, judicial and regulatory records, platform-published rate data and directory listings, and separates that from the promotional material which currently stands in for market research on the subject. The argument is that the Indian web services market grew as a residue of two larger structures rather than under its own logic. The first is the offshore labour-arbitrage system built between 1968 and 2008. The second is the collapse of entry-level hiring in India's formal technology labour market after 2022. The paper then identifies the mechanisms behind the sector's persistent price dispersion, which are unobservable quality, near-zero entry barriers, absent contract enforcement and lead resale, and places them in the institutional conditions of Indian small business. It sets out a scenario analysis of what artificial intelligence is likely to do, stated without a prior in either direction, and closes with a selection rule for buyers facing a market in which quality cannot be observed before purchase.

detail.abstract: The expansion of decentralised finance (DeFi) into real-world assets (RWAs) remains constrained by the absence of verifiable, standardised, and privacy-preserving compliance infrastructures. While DeFi protocols enable trustminimised execution and programmable financial logic, they lack mechanisms to reliably validate off-chain information such as ownership, provenance, and source of funds, which are essential for integrating institutional-grade assets. This paper presents a blockchain-based trust infrastructure designed to address this gap, using real estate transactions as a representative use case. The proposed system formalises due diligence workflows through smart contracts that encode asset registration, documentation scoring, and role-based negotiation within a permissioned ledger. Built using DAML, the architecture reflects established legal responsibilities, using the UK conveyancing process as a representative example, while enabling traceability, auditability, and a standardised assessment of transaction readiness. A key innovation is the introduction of a scoring mechanism whereby legal professionals evaluate the completeness and reliability of property documentation, producing a quantifiable metric that can be consumed by other system participants. This transforms compliance from a document-based process into a structured, machine-interpretable signal. The architecture further supports integration with zero-knowledge proofs, enabling verification of compliance conditions without disclosure of sensitive data. We show how this framework can function as a compliance and verification layer for tokenised RWAs, enabling on-chain issuance, programmable transfers, and collateralisation within DeFi environments. Scenario-based testing demonstrates that all contract interactions are logged, versioned, and attributable to defined roles, ensuring both transparency and accountability. The proposed system contributes to the emerging literature on RWA infrastructure by providing a practical, regulatorily aligned pathway for integrating real-world assets into decentralised financial systems, where it can be interpreted as a compliance and verification layer.

detail.abstract: Generative and agentic AI are changing knowledge work at the level of entire workflows; in software development and code-intensive research, a single human request can trigger extended sequences of retrieval, generation, tool use, testing, debugging, and revision. Such systems can reduce production effort while increasing validation, integration, coordination, and maintenance burdens, making conventional measures such as code generated or time saved incomplete or inaccurate productivity indicators. We argue that the appropriate unit of design is the AI-mediated workflow: an end-to-end configuration of human and AI activity through which objectives become valuable outcomes. We develop three desiderata: productivity should be measured across multiple dimensions as realized end-to-end value; workflow redesign should reallocate tasks, evidence, attention, decision rights, and accountability; and human capability should be treated as a dynamic state variable that AI-mediated work can strengthen or erode over time. We propose a three-layered intervention stack that jointly optimizes AI execution, interaction, and governance.

detail.abstract: The consumer economy runs in part on attention rent: margin that sellers extract because human buyers search a little, remember imperfectly, and respond to persuasion. As personal purchasing agents ("twins") take over consumer choice, the standard expectation is that this rent collapses. We model a market with a mixed population of human and agent buyers in which sellers choose price, consumer-directed advertising, and agent-directed optimization spend, and we show that the collapse is neither smooth nor complete. Four results follow from the structure of agent demand. First, because a well-informed agent's demand is close to winner-take-most in quality-adjusted price, sellers face a discrete choice between a human-exploiting price and an agent-competitive one, which produces a tipping point: in our simulations gross margin falls 1.4 percentage points as the agent share rises from 0 to 0.2, then drops from 40% to 33% by a share of 0.3 and to 4% when all buyers are agents. Second, we prove that in a duopoly benchmark a mixed population admits no pure-strategy equilibrium in the interior of a discrete price grid — a counterpart of Varian (1980), subject to a grid-fineness condition we state — and in the simulated market every convergent run sits at one of the two boundaries, which is what that mechanism predicts. Third, if agents are persuadable, advertising does not disappear but migrates: total persuasion spending peaks at 1.69 times the pre-agent advertising budget and remains above it when all buyers are agents. That migration does not chiefly misallocate demand — good sellers still win about 85% of sales either way — but it preserves seller rent (margin 9.9% against 4.0%) and concentrates the market by a factor of 2.4 (HHI 7,424 against 3,102). Consumer net value per unit also falls, and across the persuadability range it crosses from positive to negative in the neighbourhood of gamma = 1; we report that crossing rather than a percentage change, because the level of that series is an artifact of the value scale (Appendix C). Fourth, we measure the parameter the third result turns on. In a preregistered experiment of 18,000 purchase decisions across three frontier LLMs acting as buyers, one sentence of unverifiable promotional text raises a mid-ranked product's selection rate by a factor of 8 to 14, while a length-matched neutral placebo shows no detectable effect (z = -0.04, +1.18, +1.25) — and the share going to the genuinely best-value product falls on every model. A second preregistered experiment of 19,200 further decisions finds that this susceptibility does not detectably change when the buying instruction states urgency. Persuadability is therefore not an assumption of this paper but a measured property of the models tested. We also read the agentic-commerce protocols standardized between 2025 and 2026 — AP2, ACP, Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol, Mastercard Agent Pay and UCP — and find that they cryptographically secure payment authorization while leaving product claims unstructured and unattested, lowering the friction that governs adoption without touching the parameter that governs who captures the gains. Simulation code, both preregistrations, and all 37,200 measured decisions are public at https://github.com/sage7AI-explore/after-attention.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly influencing economic development, public services, and geopolitical influence, posing an important governance challenge to African countries. This policy research looks at AI governance through the prism of digital sovereignty, saying that African countries should not merely copy regulatory frameworks produced by external powers. Instead, governance frameworks should reflect African economic, social, cultural, and institutional conditions while also promoting technological growth. The report examines Zambia, Rwanda, Kenya, and South Africa in terms of AI policy, digital infrastructure, data governance, research, innovation, and institutional capacity. It contends that genuine digital sovereignty involves more than just regulation: African countries must build the infrastructure, computing power, skills, research ecosystems, and data governance institutions required to participate in AI development and reap more benefits from it. The study concludes with four recommendations for African AI governance: infrastructure, data governance, continental cooperation, and investment in African talent and innovation.

detail.abstract: Large language models now produce linguistic forms that circulate within human sign practices without having been written by anyone. This essay proposes a conceptual vocabulary for that phenomenon. It introduces the notion of the generative inscription-an automatically produced trace that is reinserted into the archive of human writing without originating in an embodied, accountable subject-and argues that the circulation of such inscriptions constitutes a regime of hybrid semiosis: a composite sign process in which the production of plausible linguistic configurations has been technically exteriorized, while interpretation, warrant, and responsibility remain irreducibly human. The device that sustains this regime is characterized as a techno-semiotic machine, understood as neither an artificial mind nor an inert computational tool. The argument draws its principal interpretive resources from the work of Carlo Sini on writing, technics, and sign practices, read alongside Peircean semiotics and recent debate in the philosophy of technology. The essay develops the account through an analysis of the language model as a writing machine and an operative archive, and then applies it to understanding, hallucination, prompting, alignment, and distributed authorship. It concludes by arguing that the relevant unit of philosophical analysis is neither the model nor the user, but the hybrid practice constituted through their interaction, and by outlining the conditions of responsible co-writing that follow from this.

detail.abstract: Deep uncertainty and non-linear disturbances challenge controlling approaches centered on predefined targets, periodic reporting and prediction. This article develops a conceptual model of controlling as non-linear and symbiotic navigation in the BANI environment. Drawing on controlling theory, the resource-based perspective and human–AI symbiosis, it reconceptualizes controlling as non-linear navigation in organizational homeoresis: maintaining identity and developmental continuity while permitting changes in goals and resource configurations. The model integrates event-driven readiness, non-linear feedforward and monitoring of cumulative allostatic load. It assigns sensing, simulation and bounded execution to AI (operating in symbiosis with a human), epistemic governance to the controller, and strategic authorization and responsibility to the manager, distinguishing Human-on-the-loop from Human-in-the-loop decision regimes. A synthetic proof-of-concept simulation using H3LIX OS, as the operating system enabling human-AI symbiosis, compares the proposed solution with classical and KPI-only algorithmic controlling across 10,000 disturbance sequences in a simulated regional microgrid. The homeorhetic corridor was preserved in 80.02% of runs, compared with 22.78% and 31.01%, respectively. These model-dependent findings illustrate the operationalization of the proposed new approach to controlling. The main contribution of the paper is an integrated framework of non-linear and symbiotic controlling connecting dynamic resilience, organizational identity and governed human–AI decision-making under BANI conditions.

title: Super-Optimization: When Optimization Outpaces the Capacity for Double-Loop Revision

detail.title: Super-Optimization: When Optimization Outpaces the Capacity for Double-Loop Revision

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: Super-intelligence's founding definition describes a capability level, not a rate-but one of the central fears attached to the concept is a rate claim: that capability can outrun our capacity to remain oriented to it. This paper argues that optimization has a corresponding failure mode. A goal-directed system possesses at least two capacities: the capacity to optimize an operative objective (O), and the capacity to remain oriented to that objective's adequacy, meaning, and revisability (R). Argyris and Schön named the qualitative distinction between these in 1974 as single-loop and double-loop learning; March, independently, showed in 1991 that adaptive processes can refine exploitation faster than exploration, with short-run gains and long-run costs. Neither formalizes the specific relationship this paper proposes: that O and R can diverge in proportional growth rate-d(log O)/dt > d(log R)/dt-in any goal-directed system, not only organizations with reflective human members, and that R itself separates into an epistemic component (recognizing that an objective needs revision) and a governance component (holding the standing to actually revise it), which can diverge from each other as well as from O. The paper distinguishes the resulting construct, Super-Optimization, from suboptimization, goal displacement, Goodhart effects, requisite variety, exploration and exploitation, and scalable AI oversight; grounds the mechanism in independent organizational-learning literature and in Miller's Icarus Paradox and NASA's Challenger and Columbia losses; distinguishes epistemic revision capacity from a separate transmission interface through which it must reach governance authority to matter, evidenced by the documentary record of the 1945 Franck Report and Szilard petition and, more tentatively, by the contested 2023-2026 regulatory record of Silicon Valley Bank's failure; and proposes a three-arm test design intended to make the divergence empirically visible rather than merely historically illustrated. The framework's most immediate contemporary instance may not be any single AI system's own objective, but the organizations building them-entities whose product capabilities can scale far faster than their own capacity to revise the commercial and safety objectives directing that scaling, a possibility this paper raises rather than establishes. If super-intelligence is the fear that increasingly capable systems will optimize objectives we can no longer question, Super-Optimization is the observation that this has already been happening, more slowly, for as long as goal-directed systems have existed-and that "super" need not mean better.

detail.abstract:
ABSTRACT

Legitimacy theory is arguably the most popular framework in accounting.  Ironically, it may also be the least developed.  As the first of a two-part study, the present focus is theory development.  As theory relies upon empirical study for validation, the present focus is upon laying the foundation for robust, empirical trials of legitimacy themes.  In support of an ambitious research objective, the quest for robust, theoretical insights benefts from path redundancy.  The initial path applies a comprehensive Root Cause Analysis (RCA) to systematically evaluate the leading causes of theoretical dormancy in this domain.  To promote reliability, the RCA-analysis draws from the universe of published research on legitimacy, domain inclusive. 

The second strategy, no less robust than the first, exploits cross-domain validation to glean generous, theoretical insights into legitimacy.  As an innovative study approach, it capitalizes on the close conceptual convergence between legitimacy and robust, empirical constructs from alternative domains (e.g., Signal Theory; Identity; and Organizational Bias).  The original approach to legitimacy makes noteworthy contributions in several areas.  However, the primary learning advancement is a positivist (i.e., theoretical) model of legitimacy.  When benchmarked against the research status quo, legitimacy is unmasked as corporate power.  As theory is fecund, the present study also affords generous contexts for the empirical study of legitimacy.

detail.abstract:
Prediction markets have become multibillion-dollar platforms for putting a price on uncertainty in politics, sports, finance, and even war. States and the federal government are fighting to establish regulatory authority over them. But what happens if one becomes insolvent?
     Prediction markets depend on contingent event contracts whose value may turn on disputed facts, manipulable information, and uncertain legal status. A court confronting a failed prediction market may therefore need to resolve not only what law applies, but also what happened, before it can value the estate at all. At the same time, prediction markets strain ordinary bankruptcy doctrine governing the debtor, claim classification and priority, executory contracts, and dispute settlement.
     This uncertainty extends beyond doctrine to whether ordinary bankruptcy rules apply at all. If event contracts are derivatives—as the federal government argues—the Bankruptcy Code’s financial contract safe harbors may switch off some of bankruptcy’s central protections. If state efforts to outlaw many event contracts succeed, bankruptcy itself may be unavailable.
     These issues shed light on broader debates in bankruptcy theory. They challenge the growing reliance on market prices as evidence of value and cast doubt on whether specialized resolution regimes designed for financial institutions translate to claims whose factual and legal predicates remain unsettled. To keep bankruptcy judges from making consequential policy decisions during a freefall bankruptcy, this Article advocates for an insolvency-aware framework that regulates event contracts based on their economic function.

detail.abstract: The growing use of digital technologies in the management of construction projects has been intended to improve the ability to manage projects as well as make decisions about them; however, a number of organizations have difficulty converting their adoption of digital technology into tangible improvements in the performance of their projects. The purpose of this study is to determine the effect of digital project management tools on the three main aspects of managing the scope of a construction project, the scheduling accuracy of a construction project, and the cost control of a construction project, and identify the organizational factors which facilitate the successful adoption of new technologies. To achieve these goals, a mixed-methods research approach was used for this study. The mixed-methods research approach consisted of quantitative data collected through a survey instrument completed by construction professionals (n=50), and qualitative data collected through open-ended questions completed by industry practitioners (n=26). Descriptive statistics were used to provide a description of the frequency of occurrence of each variable studied. Correlation analysis was used to establish a relationship between variables. Regression modeling was used to test hypotheses concerning the relationship between independent variables and dependent variables. Thematic analysis was used to provide context to the results of the quantitative data collection by examining the themes or patterns in the qualitative data related to the challenges of implementing digital project management tools and the necessary conditions required to realize the benefits of digital project management tools. The results of this study indicated that digital technologies can positively impact the performance of project management processes when they are consistently deployed as part of normal business operations. The results of this study also identified leadership support, workforce capabilities, system integration, and data transparency as key elements that must be addressed in order to realize the full potential of digital project management tools. Overall, the results of this study demonstrate that achieving successful digital transformation in the construction industry requires both the adoption of digital technologies and an organization's ability to implement and utilize those technologies effectively.

detail.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are rapidly entering defense and security applications, from tactical decision support and wargaming to autonomous uncrewed systems. It is unclear how these models are applied across the defense and security domain, which technical approaches predominate, and how mature the reported work is. Existing surveys cover defense AI broadly or LLM capabilities generally, but no PRISMA-based systematic review has mapped this domain's empirical record against a structured classification scheme. We systematically review the peer-reviewed empirical literature across four databases and characterize every included study with a 20-characteristic codebook spanning military application context, technical implementation, and responsible AI practices. The 56 included studies (2023 to March 2026) form a gradient from descriptive analytics to agentic and autonomous systems, with systems holding direct control authority remaining a minority (9 of 56). The technical profile is shallow: 91% of studies are proofs of concept, prompt-engineered commercial models dominate, and responsible AI safeguards are adopted only sparsely. The codebook gives defense researchers and policymakers a reusable instrument for classifying LLM applications in defense and security, and the identified gaps mark where research and governance attention is needed next.

detail.title: Compliance Assetization and Global Stablecoin Licensing Strategy: An Institution-Based View of Cross-Border Expansion
detail.abstract: How should multinational fintech firms configure stablecoin licenses across jurisdictions when regulatory institutions are fragmented, heterogeneous, and evolving? Stablecoins have moved from crypto-native instruments toward cross-border payments and settlement, yet national licensing regimes differ sharply in ways that shape legitimacy, transaction costs, and market access. Drawing on an institution-based view of international strategy, transaction cost economics, regulatory competition theory, and institutional voids theory, we develop compliance assetization, i.e., the process through which regulatory licenses function as strategic institutional assets rather than sunk compliance costs. We combine comparative institutional analysis of fiat stablecoin licensing across 23 jurisdictions with theory-building case studies in Kenya and Kazakhstan. The analysis maps systematic variation along eight dimensions of licensing institutions and distinguishes four strategic pathways, i.e., regulatory arbitrage, legitimacy premium, institutional void substitution, and regulatory portfolio synergy. We argue that optimal licensing strategy is contingent on host-market institutional conditions, particularly whether voids are systemic or niche-specific. In emerging markets with mature domestic payment infrastructure, partnership-based niche entry tends to dominate platform replacement. Overall, the study extends international business research on institutional strategy to digitally enabled cross-border finance and explains how firms convert regulatory authorization into international expansion capability under institutional heterogeneity.

detail.abstract: This study aims to develop a comprehensive security strategy framework for public and private universities in the Kingdom of Bahrain, addressing the critical distinction between peacetime security requirements and wartime/crisis protocols. Drawing upon the Kingdom's "Security Sword Theory" and comparative analysis of higher education security models in conflict-affected contexts, this study examines the structural, cybernetic, and cognitive dimensions of university security. A mixed-methods strategic analysis design is employed, integrating document analysis of institutional selfevaluation reports, comparative benchmarking against international models, and strategic inference of potential threat scenarios. Findings reveal that Bahraini universities possess foundational peacetime security infrastructure-including surveillance systems, health units, and information security protocols-yet lack structured transition protocols for wartime conditions. The study identifies three critical gaps: (1) absence of emergency response manuals governing document evacuation and crisis cell formation; (2) insufficient advanced cybersecurity architecture capable of resisting sophisticated threats; and (3) underdeveloped cognitive security mechanisms to counter psychological operations targeting university communities. The study proposes the "Academic Shield Model," a five-layer integrated framework encompassing dynamic physical defense, advanced cyber defense, cognitive immunity, social cohesion, and expanded security coordination with national defense entities. This model offers a strategic roadmap for universities in the Kingdom of Bahrain to achieve resilience across the full spectrum of peacetime and wartime conditions.

detail.abstract:
This article investigates why the tax nexus expanded so rapidly in recent decades and, more specifically, whether this expansion can be understood as a consequence of the weakening of informational and enforcement constraints that traditionally limited this exercise. 

The scholarly literature has devoted considerable attention to the competing economic, technological, legal and normative considerations invoked to justify the expansion of the tax nexus, particularly in cases in which taxing rights are asserted over persons, property, conduct or circumstances lacking a territorial-physical connection with the taxing State. This article takes a different approach. It argues that although these considerations help explain why States have sought to expand the nexus, they do not, by themselves, explain how such an expansion became practically possible. The key determinant of the expansion lies in international administrative cooperation and, more specifically, in the progressive weakening of the informational and enforcement constraints that had previously limited the exercise of taxing rights beyond the State's territorial-physical reach. International administrative cooperation thus changed the practical conditions under which sovereignty could be exercised and provided the conditions necessary for the expansion of the tax nexus, particularly in relation to the market-based nexus. 

The article, therefore, advances a two-dimensional account of nexus expansion. In addition to considerations relating to digitalisation and globalisation, tax competition, fairness, and economic allegiance, it identifies changes in international administrative cooperation, particularly the weakening of informational and enforcement constraints, as a conditio sine qua non for understanding how that expansion became practically possible. 

This revised two-step understanding of the expansion requires a word of caution. Given that the latest expansions of the source nexus require cooperation from the State where the taxpayer, information, or assets are physically located, such cooperation should be seen as the infrastructure that enables this exercise. And such cooperation rests on reciprocal political commitments that can be revised at any time. 

Tax nexus expansion is, in a certain way, a continuation by other means of the (inherent) State impulse to extend power and sovereignty, now pursued through tax claims rather than territorial claims. Accordingly, an expansion perceived as an excessive intrusion into another State's fiscal sovereignty risks eroding the very cooperative infrastructure that sustains it. A paradox that may ultimately limit how far the tax nexus can expand in practice.

detail.abstract: This thesis addresses the problematic ‘legal’ and protection gap of environmental displacement endemic to the climate-change-vulnerable (or “vulnerablised”) regions of Africa. This is undertaken in three specific but interrelated ways. Firstly, the thesis focuses the latitude of its analysis on the particularly or maximally vulnerable regions of the Horn of Africa and the Sahel, delineating the need for adaptive and mitigative activity as well as a coordinated and well-systematised institutive response suitably designed to the specific circumstances and exigencies of displaced Africans. Secondly, the thesis engages in a critical assessment of existing legal regimes, conventions, policies, and norms in the context of conventional modes of protection throughout the law of stateless persons, refugee and asylum, and human rights. Consequently, the thesis argues that these modes exhibit three specific legal shortfalls which render the protection of environmentally displaced Africans particularly problematic: (1), the law of stateless persons only applies in a matter of high extremes of uncertainty, and is insufficient regardless, rendering an issue of contingency. (2), existing refugee and asylum regimes both fail to conceptually accommodate environmentally displaced persons as a matter of conventional practice and prospective amendment, rendering an issue of applicability. (3), though human rights law provides a useful groundwork for protection and enjoys some applicability, it merely provides weak and ambiguous baseline protections which can be repudiated at any time, do not institute any protected status, and fail to accommodate the specific circumstances of environmentally displaced persons. Consequently, this mode renders an issue of functionality. Accordingly, this thesis endeavours to emend this wide shortfall of existing regimes by sketching a threefold remedial rights-oriented, integrative framework. Firstly, the framework petitions the need and designs the means to hold states formally accountable for environmental harms as a matter of international law. Secondly, the framework argues for such established harms to be redressed in the form of an injunctive indemnity establishing a positive duty of states to the protection of affected persons. This indemnity has twofold functions: (1) an active and (2) a passive capacity. While the active capacity renders a positive duty to protection, the passive capacity establishes an operational interface from which to prioritise causative environmental harms as a matter of human rights, requiring and facilitating the engagement of states on a good-faith-basis with the positive duty. Thirdly and finally, to ossify this approach and precipitate its establishment as a tenable legal regime, the framework requires the drafting and institution of a universal paradigm in the form of a quasi-legal instrument, enabling the applicable state to retain jurisdictional capacities while also fulfilling intergovernmental obligations to a satisfactory degree.

detail.title: The Structure and Performance of the Herbal Medicine Market in Ghana: Actors, Marketing Channels and Market Constraints
detail.abstract: Herbal medicine constitutes an important component of Ghana’s healthcare and livelihood systems. The increasing commercialisation of herbal medicine has created a complex market involving producers, input providers, traders and consumers. The structure and the performance of the market remain inadequately documented. This study examined the structure and the performance of the herbal medicine market in Ghana, focusing on the major market actors, marketing channels and constraints affecting market performance. A cross-sectional mixed-methods research design was adopted. Data were collected from 290 respondents comprising 24 input providers, 193 herbal medicine producers/practitioners and 73 traders. Structured questionnaires, semi-structured interviews and direct observations were used for data collection. Quantitative data were analysed using frequencies, percentages and cross-tabulations, while qualitative information was analysed thematically. The findings revealed that herbal medicine marketing involved a differentiated structure in which input providers supplied medicinal plants and other production materials, producers/practitioners performed production and processing functions, and traders facilitated wholesale and retail distribution. The marketing channels identified were producer to consumer, producer to trader(wholesaler), and trader to consumer channels. The direct channel was associated with greater price control and higher perceived profitability, whereas the intermediary-based channel provided wider market reach. The study further found that limited access to finance, transportation difficulties, inadequate storage facilities and irregular availability of medicinal plant materials as well as limited market information constrained market performance. The study recommends government and other organizations should strengthen access to finance, improving market infrastructure and information systems. Also, the ministry of health should promote sustainable medicinal plant sourcing, and providing supportive regulatory mechanisms could improve marketing efficiency, strengthen the bargaining position of market actors and enhance the overall performance and sustainability of Ghana’s herbal medicine sector.

detail.abstract: We study exact choice-oracle testing of substitutability in the setting of matching with contracts. Our first result sharpens the known exponential lower bound: At the identity choice function Cⁱᵈ(A) = A on n contracts, every substitutability certificate relative to the class of choice functions rationalized by strict preference orders over bundles and satisfying the law of aggregate demand must include the queries at all 2ⁿ − 2 nonempty proper menus. Hence, every randomized tester for the stated class with two-sided error at most ε makes at least (1 − 2ε)(2ⁿ − 2) expected queries at Cⁱᵈ. By contrast, under irrelevance of rejected contracts and bounded capacity at most q, every failure of substitutability is witnessed on a menu of size at most q + 2, which means that substitutability testing is polynomial in n for fixed q.

detail.abstract:
Capital projects frequently experience avoidable cost, schedule, and execution problems when engineering requirements and supply-market realities are not aligned early enough in the project lifecycle. Engineering may define technically appropriate requirements without sufficient visibility into supplier capacity, lead times, cost drivers, or available alternatives, while supply chain may identify market constraints or opportunities only after design decisions have become difficult and costly to change. This paper presents a practitioner-developed framework for improving early coordination between engineering and supply chain at both the project and procurement-package levels.

The framework consists of five complementary practices: (1) involving supply chain during front-end engineering and design (FEED) to inform package strategy and identify supply constraints; (2) applying a DEEK (Design, Engineering, Estimating, Kickoff) readiness gate before major packages are released to the market; (3) using a READ (Recognize, Evaluate, Anticipate, Develop) matrix to convert cross-functional issues into defined actions; (4) establishing project-level governance through a RACI alongside package-level responsibility assignments through a Materials/Package Responsibility Matrix (MRM); and (5) using a balanced scorecard that explicitly identifies functional trade-offs and agreed decision boundaries.

The framework was developed and refined through practitioner experience across capital projects in energy, mining, battery materials, and advanced manufacturing. Illustrative templates for the DEEK gate, project-level RACI, package-level MRM, and balanced scorecard are provided to support practical implementation. Field observations indicate potential improvements in procurement cycle time, sourcing efficiency, and cost outcomes when technical requirements, supply-market conditions, and decision ownership are addressed before competitive bidding. However, the reported observations are based on practitioner experience and portfolio-level before-and-after comparisons rather than controlled comparative studies. The paper therefore presents the framework as a field-built implementation approach and identifies controlled measurement of procurement cycle time, engineering changes, change orders, supplier lead-time variance, and Total Installed Cost as areas for future validation.

detail.title: Macroeconomic Impacts of China’s Energy Transition
detail.abstract: Solar and wind power account for a growing share of electricity generation in China and now dominate new capacity additions. As the power system transitions toward renewable generation, greater flexibility will be required to maintain system stability. This paper uses a computable general equilibrium model to assess the macroeconomic implications of this transition. Model results indicate a modest increase in electricity prices in the near-term, followed by sustained declines as renewable shares rise, particularly when variability is managed through battery storage rather than coal-fired backup generation. While the transition requires substantial adjustments in electricity supply and investment, it raises GDP in the long run and strengthens energy security. Battery-based flexibility outperforms continued reliance on coal across multiple dimensions, even when accounting for rising electricity demand from emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence. However, this transition pathway also increases the risk of stranded assets in the coal power sector.

title: When Compliance Becomes a Signal: Optical Compliance, Supervisory Design, and the Economics of Evidence

detail.title: When Compliance Becomes a Signal: Optical Compliance, Supervisory Design, and the Economics of Evidence
detail.abstract: This paper argues that firms do not merely respond to regulatory rules; they respond to what supervisors are observed to reward. Where supervisory attention — by regulators over firms, and by second- and third-line functions over the first line — weighs governance artefacts and personal credibility more heavily than independent evidence of operating effectiveness, firms rationally optimise toward the signals being measured, producing what this paper terms optical compliance: the visible appearance of control without its substance. The same mechanism recurs at each layer of the supervisory chain, from the business through compliance and the board to the regulator itself, because every layer's own effectiveness is, in turn, judged partly through governance signals rather than direct observation. This is a variant of Goodhart's Law applied to supervision itself. The paper develops this mechanism across four connected deficiencies — artefact substitution, the credibility trap, episodic "tsunami-like" supervision, and the feedback loop that turns supervisory habit into industry best practice — before arguing that AI-enabled monitoring is beginning to change the underlying economics by sharply reducing the cost of operating evidence, and therefore the value of credibility as a substitute for it. The paper closes with implications for C-suite strategy and a stakeholder-by-stakeholder response, from the regulator through to the embedded risk advisor.

detail.title: FireInSite: an Accessible, Integrated Fire Behaviour Prediction System for the UK and Ireland
detail.abstract: Accessible tools to support wildfire management are lacking for humid temperate regions. We developed FireInSite as a user-oriented system for predicting fire behaviour for major fire-prone fuels at any location in the UK and Ireland. Extensive fuel moisture, flammability, and seasonally varying energy content data underpin FireInSite’s integrated fuel moisture, heat content, and fuel modules. The user-friendly interface requires no user input to generate fire behaviour predictions, other than selecting a location of interest or using the automatic geolocated selection. It does so by characterising the state of the fuels of interest at any point in the season in respect to a location's climatology and weather as novel modules and then directing the relationships between these modules into a fire behaviour prediction model based on the Rothermel family of equations. As well as hourly forecasts, hindcasts of fire behaviour are also available back to 1970 and weather and fuel moisture forecasts can be compared to historical conditions. FireInSite therefore enables assessment of fire risk, effects of fuel load reduction, or planning for fire prevention and suppression. FireInSite has been used by Fire and Rescue Services and land managers in the UK and Ireland since 2025, and community response and validation have demonstrated the skill of FireInSite as a decision support tool. FireInSite’s capabilities therefore provide previously lacking support for the UK, Ireland, and comparable humid temperate regions, enabling them to better prepare for and mitigate their accelerating wildfire risk.

detail.abstract: Large language models generate optimization formulations, algorithms, and operational decisions. A successful solver run or a matching objective value does not by itself establish that the generated output is correct. This review asks what reliability claims the literature supports, which assumptions those claims require, and how the checks themselves are evaluated. We conduct a critical narrative review of work available through September 2026, organizing studies by the output checked, the property claimed, the evidence used, the trusted inputs, and the instances covered. We distinguish numerical agreement, behavioral testing, formal certification, statistical selection, and safeguards that restrict an output's effect. The evidence reveals three recurring limitations. A guarantee about a formal object does not validate its translation from a user's requirements. Agreement among candidates need not expose a shared specification error. Empirical success on selected instances does not establish performance throughout a problem class. Reported checks also leave unresolved cases or reject correct outputs, but their rates have different denominators and cannot be pooled into a single reliability estimate. We compare the available evidence across formulations, algorithms, and direct decisions; clarify the difference between benchmark-label agreement and model correctness; and develop an evaluation protocol with explicit error rates, coverage, reference quality, and computational budgets. The review identifies research opportunities in independently checkable formulation benchmarks, distribution-specific evaluation of generated policies, and execution rules with proved loss bounds. Its contribution is an evidence-based account of what current checks establish and what additional evidence is needed before operational use.

detail.abstract: The traditional Three Lines of Defense (3LOD) model maintains independence and governance oversight but often incentivizes firms to produce compliance artefacts rather than address real operational risks. The Compact 3LOD Model reallocates operational tasks to embed independently-supervised advisory functions within 1LOD, concentrate independent validation — not monitoring — in 3LOD, and maintain 2LOD as an oversight and regulatory liaison function that challenges rather than performs the underlying checking. The reallocation serves three distinct design objectives, and an institution adopting the model should be explicit about which it is solving for: improving assurance efficiency by having each line do the work only it is positioned to do; strengthening the independence and credibility of the compliance function by removing it from tasks placed too close to first-line decision-making; and improving first-line risk and compliance capability directly, through a Risk Advisory presence that observes, coaches, and corrects. The first and third objectives are often best served by a capability that recedes once its purpose is met; the second is a structural safeguard an institution may reasonably wish to hold in place indefinitely. The distinction is addressed further in the accompanying Implementation Guide. Here, verifiable assurance means assurance whose conclusions can be independently supported from source evidence, rather than merely from another reviewer’s account.

detail.abstract: An isolation of a positive definite integral lattice f represents every proper full-rank sublattice of f but not f itself. detail.abstract:
Background: Treatment interruption is commonly defined as >28 days without an expected ART pickup or clinical contact, but earlier tracing could increase workload. We evaluated the workload–lead-time trade-off at earlier tracing thresholds.

Methods: We analyzed national ART dispensing data from Kenya, 2017–23. Gap episodes were defined from estimated ART supply end to return, comparing >7-, >14-, >21-, and >28-day thresholds. Using each patient’s first gap >7 days, we estimated PPV (proportion progressing beyond day 28), alerts per interruption, lead time, and facility workload. Secondary analyses assessed variation by dispensing duration and facility, and viral non-suppression by gap duration.

Findings: Among 838,306 people contributing 10,444,801 dispensing episodes, 796,675 had a first gap >7 days and 576,041 (72·3%) progressed beyond day 28. PPV increased from 72·3% at day 7 to 84·0% at day 14 and 91·2% at day 21, while alerts per interruption decreased from 1·38 to 1·19 and 1·10. Compared with day 28, day 14 provided 14 additional days for intervention with 2·9 additional alerts per facility-month; moving to day 7 gained 7 further days but approximately doubled the additional workload. Day-7 PPV was 51·6% with ≥6-month dispensing versus ≥69·8% with shorter intervals. Viral non-suppression was highest after 15–21-day gaps.

Interpretation: The >28-day definition of treatment interruption need not determine when tracing starts. Day 14 provided a pragmatic balance between workload and lead time, with thresholds potentially adapted to dispensing duration and local capacity.

title: A Cloud-Native MLOps Framework for Reproducible Deployment and Drift Monitoring of Clinical Deep Learning Models
affiliations: San Francisco Bay University and Southern Arkansas University

detail.title: A Cloud-Native MLOps Framework for Reproducible Deployment and Drift Monitoring of Clinical Deep Learning Models
detail.abstract: Background and Objective: Clinical deep learning models are typically validated once, at the point of regulatory clearance, yet the populations, instruments and clinical workflows they operate on continue to change after deployment. Reporting guidelines and regulators increasingly ask for an explicit, auditable monitoring and retraining plan, but few published pipelines couple statistical drift detection to an actual retraining policy and measure the resulting diagnostic-accuracy consequences end to end, including the cases in which monitoring fails. We present and empirically validate a cloud-native MLOps framework that does so on two public clinical prediction tasks.,Methods: The framework combines a content-addressable model registry with full data/code/model lineage, a four-detector drift-monitoring ensemble (Kolmogorov-Smirnov testing with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery control, the Population Stability Index, kernel Maximum Mean Discrepancy, and a classifier two-sample test) combined by majority vote, and a confirmation-gated retraining policy that warm-starts fine-tuning on an expanding labelled window rather than discarding the historical training population. We validated the pipeline on feed-forward classifiers trained on the UCI Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer and Pima Indians Diabetes datasets, subjecting each to a controlled deployment simulation with covariate-, label- and concept-shift injection, and two stationary control streams, modelled on the dataset-shift validation protocol of Rabanser et al.,Results: Baseline models reached test AUROC 0.999 (95% CI 0.997-1.000) on WDBC and 0.810 (95% CI 0.724-0.887) on PIMA. The monitoring ensemble detected 3 of 6 injected shifts with a consistent one-batch delay and raised zero confirmed false alarms across 21 stationary control batches, while all covariate- and label-shift detections triggered retraining that left diagnostic performance unchanged or modestly improved (AUROC delta -0.010 to +0.027). Concept drift, by contrast, was undetected in both datasets and coincided with the largest true performance losses observed (AUROC drop of 0.53 in WDBC and 0.23 in PIMA), a structural blind spot of any feature-only monitor rather than an implementation defect.,Conclusions: A feature-space drift ensemble reliably catches covariate and label shift and its associated retraining does no measurable harm, but it cannot see the shift that hurt performance most in these experiments, motivating outcome- or performance-based monitoring as a mandatory complement rather than an optional extra in any clinical MLOps deployment.

detail.abstract: Acquired drug resistance in cancer develops progressively rather than instantaneously, with regulatory rewiring of lncRNA-miRNA competing-endogenous-RNA networks occurring over the course of treatment rather than as a single static event. Existing computational models of this process either model temporal dynamics without an explicit, mechanistically-motivated lncRNA-miRNA cross-attention structure (the closest prior work uses a hierarchical graph autoencoder with LSTM-based dose conditioning), or model lncRNA-miRNA regulatory interactions without any temporal dimension. This paper proposes a Cross-Attention Transformer that models regulatory interaction between lncRNA and miRNA expression at each timestep via cross-attention, and models how this regulatory axis evolves via causal temporal self-attention across timesteps, to predict eventual resistance phenotype from an observed trajectory. Because no real time-course single-cell dataset was available in this working environment, the architecture is implemented and evaluated as a proof-of-concept (PoC) on a synthetic trajectory dataset modeling ceRNA-style coevolution, using hand-derived backpropagation verified against numerical gradients (no GPU deep-learning framework was installable in this sandboxed environment). A 5-seed replication with paired significance testing finds no statistically detectable benefit from either the cross-attention mechanism (p = 0.345) or the temporal self-attention mechanism (p = 0.503) individually, extending a pattern observed across two companion proof-of-concept papers in this research program in which specific attention/gating mechanisms have not yet shown robust ablation benefits at small synthetic scale. A genuinely informative finding, independent of the ablation result, is that the full model's ability to predict eventual resistance is near chance using only the first third of the observed trajectory and reaches its performance plateau only once roughly five of six timesteps are observed, a concrete, testable characterization of how much temporal observation this task requires. We report all results transparently and specify the real time-course data needed to properly validate the architecture.

detail.abstract: Business continuity increasingly depends on the capacity to anticipate supply chain disruption before operational thresholds are breached. This article examines how machine learning based predictive analytics can strengthen continuity and resilience across sourcing, production, logistics and recovery decisions. A structured integrative review synthesises peer reviewed studies and authoritative frameworks published principally between 2019 and 2025, supplemented by foundational resilience research. The analysis distinguishes prediction from resilience: a model creates continuity value only when its output is converted into timely, feasible and governed action. Five capability clusters are identified: multi-source disruption sensing, probabilistic demand and lead-time forecasting, supplier and network vulnerability estimation, scenario-based intervention selection, and post-event learning. The synthesis indicates that ensemble learning, graph-based models, anomaly detection and digital twins can improve warning quality and decision speed, but performance deteriorates under sparse disruption data, concept drift, opaque supplier tiers and biased labels. A reliability-aware architecture is therefore proposed in which every prediction is accompanied by data-quality checks, calibrated uncertainty, consequence-weighted thresholds and human escalation. The findings further show that resilience should be evaluated through service continuity, time to recover, time to survive and avoided loss rather than predictive accuracy alone. The article contributes an integrated decision framework linking machine learning outputs to continuity playbooks and identifies governance, interoperability and organisational learning as conditions for responsible adoption. Practical implications are offered for firms seeking measurable resilience without replacing managerial judgement with automated confidence.

detail.abstract: Service Level Objectives (SLOs) for Spark data pipelines are conventionally validated retrospectively, through production monitoring, rather than proactively, through deliberate testing under adverse conditions before deployment. Chaos engineering, the discipline of injecting controlled failures to build confidence in a system's behavior under stress offers a proactive alternative, but has not, to the authors' knowledge, been formalized specifically as a methodology for pre-production SLO validation in Spark data platforms. This paper proposes chaos engineeringaugmented SLO testing: a methodology in which a portfolio of resilience configurations (checkpoint interval, replication factor, speculative execution, spare executor capacity) is evaluated against a curated suite of injected failure scenarios (executor kills, network latency, disk I/O throttling, shuffle-service failures) before deployment, using a machine learning surrogate model to predict SLO-violation risk across configurations too numerous to test exhaustively. Building on the cost-aware right-sizing approach of Mohammed, Bohra, and Soni (2026), the methodology treats resilience investment as a configuration decision with both a steady-state cost and a chaosconditional reliability benefit, analogous to but distinct from that prior work's cost-performance right-sizing problem. Because real production chaos-experiment datasets are not available for academic research, the study is conducted as a synthetic-data proof-of-concept: a surrogate violation-prediction model (AUC = 0.945 on held-out job types) is used to select a chaos-informed resilience configuration for each of a portfolio of held-out jobs, evaluated against a separate, unseen distribution of "production" failure scenarios. The chaos-informed selection process is shown to meaningfully differentiate jobs by their actual sensitivity to injected failures (correlation of 0.665 between a job's shuffle intensity and its selected resilience level), producing a continuously tunable trade-off between steadystate cost and production violation rate rather than forcing a single blanket configuration across a heterogeneous job portfolio. At a strict testsuite threshold, the chaos-informed policy achieves a 7.0% cost reduction relative to a uniformly maximum-resilience baseline, at a modest, consistent increase in violation rate that holds stably across mild, baseline, and severe simulated production-incident scenarios. These results are illustrative rather than confirmatory: the workload, failure-injection, and cost models are synthetic, and the reported figures describe recovery of a known, programmed relationship rather than real-world reliability improvement. The article proposes the resulting methodology as a template for future validation using real chaos-engineering tooling and production telemetry.

detail.abstract: A companion paper ("Paper 3") reported two 5-seed ablations for a Cross-Attention Transformer modeling temporal lncRNA-miRNA regulatory dynamics: removing cross-attention (d₂ =-0.48, p = 0.345) and removing temporal selfattention (d₂ =-0.33, p = 0.503), both non-significant and both nominally favoring the simpler ablated model. A retrospective power calculation indicated these two comparisons would require approximately 34 and 73 seeds respectively to reach 80% power both underpowered, but by very different margins. This paper reruns both ablations with 40 fresh, pre-specified confirmatory seeds. The two comparisons resolve in genuinely different ways. The crossattention effect shrinks by 79% (d₂ =-0.48 to-0.10) and remains non-significant in the larger sample, consistent with the original result having been mostly sampling noise around a true effect close to zero, a properly-powered confirmed null. The temporal-attention effect, in contrast, strengthens and reaches significance (d₂ =-0.39, p = 0.018 fresh; p = 0.013 combined), in the same unfavorable direction observed in the original pilot: the causal temporal self-attention mechanism, as implemented, measurably hurts held-out performance relative to using only the final timestep's representation. We report both results plainly, including the substantive implication that a specific architectural component motivated by this research program's central framing (temporal evolution) appears, on properly-powered evidence, to be actively counterproductive rather than merely unhelpful.

detail.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as inexpensive judges to evaluate outputs, label data, and assess whether a system meets a desired quality standard. Yet using AI judgments for formal statistical inference is fundamentally different from simply treating them as ground-truth labels: AI evaluations can be biased or noisy, and rigorous hypothesis testing requires explicit control of type-I and type-II errors. We study how to use AI judgments, together with selective human verification, to conduct a valid hypothesis test at minimum cost. We consider a population of items with hidden binary labels. After choosing a fixed pool of items, the decision maker can selectively query AI, send an item directly to a human, escalate an AI-scored item to a human after observing the AI report, or stop once sufficient evidence has accumulated. We derive an information-theoretic lower bound that captures the minimum cost of achieving prescribed testing errors and characterizes the value of AI information and human verification through a report-dependent information frontier. Motivated by this characterization, we develop SCALE, a sequential cost-aware policy that combines selective AI scoring with adaptive human escalation. SCALE is valid at finite sample sizes and matches the lower bound to first order as the target error probabilities vanish. We further extend the framework to an unknown AI-output model using paired AI-human pilot data. Numerically, SCALE approaches Human-only or AI-only testing when one source clearly dominates, while achieving its largest savings when inexpensive AI judgments and selective human verification are both valuable.

title: Algorithmic Collusion by Reinforcement-Learning Pricing Agents: Simulation Evidence and Implications for Financial Markets and Competition Law

detail.title: Algorithmic Collusion by Reinforcement-Learning Pricing Agents: Simulation Evidence and Implications for Financial Markets and Competition Law
detail.abstract: Pricing algorithms built on reinforcement learning can reach supracompetitive outcomes with no agreement and no communication between the firms that deploy them. I report an independent simulation of Q-learning agents in a Bertrand oligopoly with logit demand and connect the results to competition policy for financial markets. Across 32 duopoly sessions the mean collusion index is 0.778, with a 95 per cent confidence interval of [0.735, 0.821] and per-firm profits 40 per cent above the Bertrand-Nash benchmark. Not one session ended at the competitive outcome. In a separate experiment on a common price grid, the index falls from 0.807 with two agents to 0.577 with three and 0.471 with four, while the relative profit gain over the competitive benchmark rises from 40 to 69 per cent. A forced deviation to the competitive price triggers a price war in the next period and a return to the previous level within five to seven periods. Removing the rival's past price from the state space eliminates the effect: the index drops to-0.018, with a confidence interval that contains zero, and prices settle at the static equilibrium. Coordination here follows from what the algorithm observes. Neither Section 1 of the Sherman Act nor Article 101 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union reaches conduct of this kind, and the RealPage proposed final judgment of November 2025 governs data inputs and tool design, leaving autonomous learning untouched.

detail.abstract: We study an online resource allocation problem with finitely many actions, random rewards, and bounded multidimensional random resource consumptions. We analyze the classic dynamic fluid policy, which re-solves a fluid relaxation at every state and uses the resulting optimal dual variable to approximate the continuation value. We show that, under standard non-degeneracy conditions, the value functions of the dynamic fluid policy and the optimal dynamic policy characterized by the Bellman equation admit the same asymptotic expansion: the fluid benchmark minus a common logarithmic correction term plus a uniformly bounded, policy-dependent remainder. Moreover, we explicitly characterize the coefficient of the logarithmic term. Consequently, the logarithmic term is a common correction to the fluid benchmark, and the dynamic fluid policy achieves a horizon-uniform constant optimality gap relative to the optimal online policy.

title: Salesperson Incentives and Consumer Product Returns

detail.title: Salesperson Incentives and Consumer Product Returns

detail.abstract: Consumer product returns impose substantial costs on offline retailers selling experience goods, as consumers cannot fully resolve product valuation uncertainty until after purchase. To help consumers assess fit, many retailers rely on salespeople, who are typically compensated through sales commissions, creating an incentive to close sales without regard for possible returns. A common countermeasure is commission chargebacks, which deduct commissions on returned products, but how chargeback policy should be designed jointly with refund and pricing decisions to properly influence salesperson behavior remains unexamined. We develop a game-theoretic model featuring a monopoly retailer employing a salesperson who chooses between baseline and qualifying effort by actively engaging consumers with ex-ante uncertain valuations. Qualifying effort produces an informative signal of product fit that consumers incorporate through Bayesian updating. The retailer sets price, refund, and chargeback levels to maximize expected profit subject to the salesperson's individual rationality and incentive compatibility constraints. By analyzing this tripartite retailer-salesperson-consumer structure, which extends the dyadic retailer-consumer framework standard in the returns literature, we prescribe actionable managerial insights for retailers. We show that inducing salesperson qualifying effort requires inclusive risk sharing: chargebacks alone cannot sustain qualifying effort, and must be paired with partial refunds so that the retailer distributes its unrealized revenue risk due to returns to keep all involved parties-consumers, salespeople, and the retailer-jointly accountable. The optimal chargeback-and-refund configuration depends on product characteristics affecting the retailer's unit returns cost and the informativeness of salesperson engagement. Critically, commonly deployed full-refund-full-chargeback policies may simultaneously hurt retailer profit and create tensions with the salesforce and its representatives.

title: Work-Life Balance Among Women in the Information Technology Sector in Bangalore: A Cross-Sectional Study of Occupational Strain and Organisational Support

detail.title: Work-Life Balance Among Women in the Information Technology Sector in Bangalore: A Cross-Sectional Study of Occupational Strain and Organisational Support

detail.abstract: Women in India's information technology (IT) workforce face sustained occupational demands and a disproportionate share of household and caregiving responsibilities, yet little evidence describes how these pressures relate to work-life balance (WLB) within a single, well-defined workforce after the acute conditions of the pandemic had passed. This study tested how occupational strain, organizational and family support, and caregiving responsibility relate to self-reported WLB satisfaction among women employed in IT and ITenabled companies in Bangalore, India. A cross-sectional survey was self-administered online via Google Forms to women working in Bangalore's IT sector between September 2023 and September 2024, using a non-probability convenience sample. After removing eight fully blank submissions, 107 responses were analysed. Five Likert items were combined into an Occupational Strain Index (Cronbach's α = .64). Associations were tested with Spearman correlation, the Mann-Whitney U test, and multiple linear regression; 250 open-ended comments across three items were coded thematically to contextualise the quantitative results. Reporting followed STROBE guidance for cross-sectional studies. Mean WLB satisfaction was 3.34 (SD = 0.94) on a five-point scale. Occupational strain showed the strongest association with satisfaction (ρ =-.38, p < .001) and remained the only significant predictor in a regression model that also included family support, leisure frequency, and caregiving status (b =-0.59, p < .001; R² = .22). Women with caregiving dependents reported significantly higher strain than those without (U = 1619, p = .044, r =-.24), although caregiving status alone did not differentiate satisfaction. Formal WLB policy presence, marital status, and workarrangement type showed no significant association with satisfaction at this sample size. The most frequent theme in open-ended responses was a request for greater flexibility in work location or hours (35.2% of substantive comments), followed by childcare provision, commuting relief, and menstrual leave. In this sample, subjective occupational strain, rather than the presence of a formal policy or a particular work arrangement, had the strongest relationship with WLB satisfaction. Interventions that target workload, deadline pressure, and commuting burden directly may therefore reach employee-reported WLB more effectively than expanding the policy menu alone, though the crosssectional, non-probability design limits causal and population-level inference.

title: Managing Operational Tensions in Scaling Emerging Technologies
