detail.abstract: Emerging technologies are often introduced with the promise of improving operational performance. OSCM research has therefore emphasised their potential to enhance operational efficiency and business performance (Lam et al., 2016; Xiong et al., 2025). Yet recent evidence suggests that scaling these technologies is constrained by operational tensions that emerge within and across processes (Wang et al., 2026; Zhan et al., 2025). We define operational tensions as persistent and interdependent trade-offs, such as centralisation versus decentralisation, efficiency versus flexibility, autonomy versus control, and sustainability versus profitability - that arise when new technologies reconfigure processes, resource allocation and governance structures, generating competing demands that cannot be easily reconciled (Roehrich et al., 2025). These tensions may remain relatively contained during pilots, but become amplified as technologies are scaled across functions, organisational units, supply networks and institutional contexts. Scaling increases interdependence, coordination costs and exposure to system-level risks, turning local implementation challenges into broader operational problems. AI provides a salient example. Its integration into operational decision-making shifts authority from human judgment to algorithmic systems, creating operational tensions between autonomy and control. AI can improve demand forecasting, capacity planning, and supplier selection, but it also introduces dependencies, opacity, and less transparent decision-making logic (Rana et al., 2022), as well as cybersecurity vulnerabilities in processes (Cohen et al., 2026; Jazairy et al., 2025). Its rapid expansion also places pressure on supporting infrastructures, including electricity systems and energy consumption, revealing tensions between technological advancement and sustainability constraints (Muir, 2025). These issues become more pronounced when AI scales across organisational boundaries, where standardisation, data integration and governance requirements may constrain flexibility and managerial oversight.

detail.abstract: We develop a cubic-augmented framework for forecasting Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES) in which the higher moments of returns are recovered in closed form from a cubic representation of the quantile function, and cubic-coefficient forecasts are mapped into tail-risk forecasts through two parallel routes. The framework is evaluated out of sample on eight MSCI equity indices, four developed and four emerging, over 6,880 daily observations from January 2000 to May 2026, using a rolling-window protocol with 1,000 evaluation windows at the five-day and one-day horizons. Coverage and expected-shortfall backtests show that the CAViaR-Cubic and Robust-Cubic specifications deliver correctly calibrated VaR and ES forecasts in the overwhelming majority of markets, at both coverage levels and horizons, whereas at the daily 1% level the Gaussian threshold-GARCH (TGARCH-N) benchmark is rejected in every market. The cubic forecasts dominate TGARCH-N on calibration and loss, and match the skewed-t specifications on loss while outperforming them on tail calibration, without requiring a parametric density. The results establish the cubic quantile approach as a new, stable and reliable route to VaR and ES forecasting.

detail.abstract: Agricultural biotechnology offers potential solutions to production threats, but technical effectiveness does not ensure consumer acceptance. This study examines whether the way biotechnology information is presented affects consumer preferences for orange juice. In a laboratory experiment, participants were randomly assigned to a control group, a scientific general-benefit message, a layperson general-benefit message, or a layperson message that connected biotechnology to citrus greening and the recovery of Florida citrus. Participants then completed a discrete choice experiment involving Bioengineered, Gene Edited, and Non-GMO Project Verified orange juice. Consumers discounted both biotechnology products in the absence of information. Each information treatment reduced the Bioengineered discount, while the treatments also reduced the Gene Edited discount. The context-specific message produced the smallest Bioengineered discount, although differences among the active messages were generally limited. The findings show that clear benefit communication can improve consumer valuation of agricultural biotechnology, while product and message context remain important for market acceptance.

detail.abstract: Problem definition: Print-on-demand (POD) platforms have emerged as popular online marketplaces where platforms print designs uploaded by content creators onto blank products upon receiving customer orders. Currently, POD platforms predominantly use make-to-order (MTO) production, resulting in high unit production costs. To reduce costs and enhance profitability, we propose a novel hybrid production that employs both MTO and the cost-efficient make-to-stock (MTS) simultaneously. However, the new structure of the POD supply chain introduces unique incentive complexities between platforms and creators so that the hybrid production cannot be effectively implemented. In particular, content creators typically favor a large assortment size, diluting the expected demand per design, which is unfavorable for the platform to adopt MTS. Methodology/results: We develop a newsvendor-based analytical model to examine hybrid production, identify the incentive misalignment and propose three implementation strategies to regulate assortment size. These strategies balance the platform's cost savings from MTS adoption against creators' potential profit losses due to reduced overall demand. Managerial implications: Our analysis demonstrates an approximate 13% improvement in overall system profit relative to the pure MTO production and establishes critical boundaries on platform-specific parameters that dictate whether adopting the hybrid production is advantageous.

detail.abstract: Minibus taxis provide a substantial share of daily public transport in South Africa, yet large-sample evidence on how far and how long individual vehicles operate remains limited. This paper uses 174.9 million GPS records from December 2025 to quantify daily distance, movement duration, operating span, active vehicles, time-of-day structure, and persistence among observed minibus taxis. Cleaned, time-ordered observations were aggregated into operational vehicle-days. The Gauteng selection contained 121,739 vehicle-days from 5,020 vehicles between 1 and 31 December; 100,006 vehicle-days from 4,836 vehicles met the analytical criteria. Median daily distance declined from 166 km during 1-25 December to 142 km during 26-31 December, median movement duration declined from 6.1 to 5.1 hours, and median operating span declined from 14.6 to 13.8 hours. The late-period morning profile was delayed, but the evening endpoint changed little: median movement start shifted from 07:19 to 07:43 and median end from 21:58 to 21:48. Within-vehicle day-today variation accounted for 65.2% of distance variation and 75.8% of operating-span variation. Nevertheless, extremedistance activity was concentrated: a vehicle-day above the fleet-wide 90th percentile was 6.1 times more likely after another such day than after a non-tail day. These findings support distributional and risk-based transport planning.

title: The DMA-GDPR In-between: Conflicts of Norms, Normative Redundancy, Mediated Tensions and Axiological Gaps

detail.abstract:
Legal contention has complicated how the regulatory boundaries between the Digital Markets Act (DMA) and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) are interpreted. Some DMA provisions touch upon the personal data processing activities of gatekeepers and third parties. When these mandates collide with the GDPR's rules and principles, legal uncertainty troubles both regulators and regulatory targets. The Joint Guidelines issued by the European Commission and the European Data Protection Board seek to settle these differences.

Within the academic debate, an analysis of the DMA’s provisions in light of their normative value is lacking. The paper tackles the challenge by building on the findings of legal philosophy and legal interpretation to determine how the interface takes form in the abstract and on the ground. To do this, the paper considers all DMA provisions under the lens of their potential incompatibility with the GDPR to determine whether conflicts of norms advise the consideration of the DMA as lex specialis to the GDPR. The paper finds that conflicts of norms coexist with instances of normative redundancy, settled conflicts and axiological gaps when the DMA is confronted with the rules and principles of the GDPR.

title: Emotional Regret Expected Utility and a Formal Resolution of the Allais Paradox: A Relative Rationality Theory Approach

detail.abstract: The Allais paradox remains one of the most important challenges to Expected Utility Theory, because many decision-makers prefer a certain gain in the first Allais experiment but choose the higher-payoff risky lottery when certainty is removed in the second. Under the standard monetary-consequence representation of the Allais problem, Expected Utility Theory has difficulty reconciling this pattern because identical monetary outcomes are represented as identical consequences across the two contexts, and the Independence axiom implies that the common consequences in the two Allais choices should cancel without reversing the preference ranking. This paper introduces Emotional Regret Expected Utility (EREU), within the framework of Relative Rationality Theory, as an alternative explanation of the Allais paradox. Lottery outcomes are not treated as isolated monetary payoffs; they are evaluated as emotionally adjusted consequences, represented through Decision-EAW, and compared with what the alternative lottery could have produced. Emotional weights are attached to these directional counterfactual comparisons, capturing anticipated regret, relief, rejoicing, certainty protection, and life goals. Unlike Rank-Dependent Utility, introduced by Quiggin (1982), which modifies decision weights according to the rank of outcomes within a lottery, EREU preserves linear probabilities and uses the alternative lottery as the counterfactual reference for emotionally weighted comparison. It differs from the canonical statecontingent representation of Regret Theory in its explicit decomposition of counterfactual evaluation: EREU separates the directional, comparison-specific emotional-intensity parameter 𝑤𝑖𝑗 from probability and from the utility difference, while evaluating that utility difference over Decision-EAW positions. Cross-outcome comparison itself is not claimed as novel, since Loomes and Sugden (1982) also considered statistically independent prospects. The EREU model shows that the preference A₁ ≻ B₁ for the sure gain in the first Allais experiment can arise when the emotionally weighted certainty–zero comparison is sufficiently strong relative to the highpayoff comparison. Likewise in the second experiment, B₂ ≻ A₂ can arise when, after certainty is removed, the emotionally weighted comparisons involving the €5 million outcome outweigh the emotionally weighted comparisons involving the €1 million outcome. The apparent reversal is therefore interpreted within EREU as a change in the dominant emotionally weighted counterfactual comparison rather than as a necessary consequence of nonlinear decision weighting. EREU thus provides a formal and psychologically motivated account of the Allais paradox while retaining linear probability and evaluating utility over Decision-EAW, the emotionally adjusted wealth position generated by combining the decision-maker’s pre-decision Emotional Adjusted Wealth (EAW) with the outcome-specific Emotional Adjusted Value (EAV).

detail.abstract: HVAC systems in buildings play a major role in energy use and operational carbon emissions, making reliable fault detection and diagnostics important for their efficient operation and occupant safety. However, conventional methods often face scalability challenges because they require site-specific rules, large labeled datasets, or limitedly interpretable models. In this study, we present an automated fault detection and diagnostic workflow that integrates a large language model with semantic and knowledge graphs. The proposed framework uses a semantic metadata model to represent HVAC system topology, a directed causal graph to encode physics-expected cause-and-effect relationships, and precomputed statistical evidence to guide large language model-based diagnostic inference. Rather than reasoning directly from raw sensor data, the LLM generates fault hypotheses grounded in a structured system context and quantitative evidence. We validated the workflow in a real controlled environmental chamber using a single-zone variable-air-volume air-handling unit operating under an ASHRAE Guideline 36 air-side economizer sequence. We included three representative faults: an overridden supply fan variablespeed drive, a stuck outdoor air damper, and a drifted supply air temperature sensor. Results show that the proposed workflow can identify the primary faults by interpreting cross-component interactions and fault propagation patterns. By grounding LLM reasoning in system ontology, expert knowledge, and statistical evidence, this approach improves diagnostic transparency, reduces hallucination risk, and provides a scalable pathway for AI-assisted HVAC fault diagnosis.

detail.abstract: The present study examines the relation between firms' financial performance and earnings management in an emerging market; namely, Egypt. We examine the association between firms' financial performance and earnings management from three perspectives. First, we investigate whether a firm's financial performance affects earnings management. Second, we examine whether firms with ineffective financial performance engage in earnings management practices more than firms with effective financial performance. Third, we test whether firms with ineffective financial performance manipulate their earnings to report greater earnings. Earnings management is captured by discretionary accruals. Cash flows from operations are used to indicate the level of a firm's financial performance, thus allowing the categorisation of the sample group of Egyptian firms into two sub-samples: firstly, those characterized by low cash flows (demonstrating ineffective financial performance, i.e. underperforming or low performing firms); and secondly, those characterized by high cash flows (demonstrating effective financial performance, i.e. high performing firms). We use the ordinary least square regression model of the relation between discretionary accruals and a firm's financial performance to examine whether a firm's financial performance affects earnings management. To assess whether firms with ineffective financial performance are more prone to manage earnings than their higher performing counterparts, we employ a contextual model (of the relation between discretionary accruals and a firm's financial performance) with a dummy variable approach that allows parameter shifts for underperforming firms. Finally, to test for income increasing accruals by underperforming firms, we test whether discretionary accruals are positive and significantly greater for underperforming firms than those for high performing firms. The results show that, first, earnings management is negatively associated with a firm's financial performance. Second, underperforming firms are engaged in more earnings management practices than their high performing counterparts. Third, underperforming firms have positive and considerably greater discretionary accruals than their effectively performing counterparts to elevate their reported earnings in order to hide their low financial performance. Overall, these results suggest that an Egyptian firm's financial performance may serve as a fundamental determinant of its likelihood of engaging in earnings management. Moreover, these results suggest that listed Egyptian firms utilize earnings management practices opportunistically as a way to conceal their ineffective/poor financial performance. Given the current weakness of investor protection and legal enforcement in Egypt, these results encourage policymakers to improve considerably corporate-governance mechanisms in Egypt. This study contributes to the limited research on earnings management in emerging markets, and specifically, Egypt.

detail.abstract: We study the optimal ordering problem for a continuous-time, stochastic two-product inventory model with fixed ordering costs. The objective is to minimize infinite-horizon expected discounted cost. While there have been a number of intermittent papers on this problem, a complete solution has remained elusive since Scarf (1960), who introduced Kconvexity to prove the optimality of the (s, S) policy for a single product. The main challenge arises from the failure to extend K-convexity to multiple products to resolve the non-convex, discontinuous fixed-cost structure. Even the ansatz for a two-product deterministic model in the existing literature lacks comprehensive verification. To address this long-standing open problem, we reformulate it as an impulse control problem, yielding a two-dimensional quasi-variational inequality (QVI). We use an iterative approximation scheme and a penalty method to establish the existence and uniqueness of a strong solution to the QVI. A weak verification theorem shows that the strong solution coincides with the value function. The optimal policy exhibits a (σ, S(x)) structure: when the inventory level x lies in the ordering region σ, an order is placed to the order-up-to level S(x). We employ a policy iteration algorithm to compute the optimal policy. Numerical experiments reveal that as either inventory becomes large, the other product's ordering boundary and order-up-to level approach their traditional single-product (s, S) values. In contrast, when both inventories are low, the joint ordering region expands to exploit economies of joint replenishment. Several managerial insights into how the optimal policy changes as parameters vary are obtained.

detail.abstract:
Within the growing game industry, there are some types of games that are more often linked to artistry, experimentation, and passion-driven development. These games are commonly referred to as independent games and are usually produced outside big corporate AAA game studio structures. Although independent teams may have more creative freedom, they still face several constraints. More specifically, they are often associated with smaller teams, which may include people with limited experience in developing games. At the same time, they are expected to compete with AAA giants of the industry, which operate with bigger budgets, larger teams, and stronger visibility.
     To understand how independent game studios manage to produce original pieces of work marked by high creativity while facing these limitations, this thesis asks: how are production and innovation negotiated across two independent game development settings? To answer this question, ZA/UM’s Disco Elysium and Sandfall Interactive’s Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 are analysed and compared using a qualitative comparative case study approach. Both games are European independent video games that became highly visible while being made outside AAA production practices and resource availability. However, their production histories show important differences, raising the question of how each studio handled its conditions and what this meant for the final production process. Disco Elysium came from a literary and artistic collective shaped by strong creative ambition, limited resources, and later internal conflict. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 shows a newer small-team model supported by tools, funding, publishing support, and external collaborators.
     Their analysis is based on media artefacts such as interviews, documentaries, postmortem-style features, and industry journalism. Thematic analysis is used to identify patterns in how the central concepts of the thesis are discussed during development, namely innovation and production choices, resource constraints, and external relationships. The findings suggest that innovation across the two cases was a constant negotiation of production decisions, creative ambition, team management, and responses to external factors that affected the development and release of each game. Across the two cases, the comparison showed how innovation is constructed through negotiated feasibility, or more specifically, how the two teams made the games they made under the conditions they had. Overall, this thesis understands independent innovation as negotiated feasibility.

detail.abstract: This study examines whether monthly changes in U.S. interest rates were associated with monthly gold returns from January 2020 through August 2026. The analysis combines monthly gold prices from the World Bank Commodity Price Data with the effective federal funds rate from the Federal Reserve. The merged sample contains 80 monthly observations. Gold returns and federal funds rate changes were calculated from the level series, after which Pearson correlations and ordinary least squares regressions were estimated for a same-month specification and a one-month-lagged specification. The same-month rate-change coefficient was negative but not statistically significant (beta =-3.176, p = 0.109). The onemonth-lagged coefficient was negative and statistically significant at the 5% level (beta =-3.984, p = 0.045; 95% confidence interval:-7.876 to-0.092). This result indicates that a one percentage-point increase in the effective federal funds rate was associated with an estimated 3.984 percentage-point reduction in the following month's gold return. However, the lagged model explained only 5.2% of the variation in monthly returns. Gold prices increased by 182.6% over the full sample, despite substantial changes in monetary policy. The evidence therefore provides limited support for a negative short-delay relationship between U.S. interest-rate changes and gold returns. The findings describe association rather than causation and should be interpreted alongside other determinants of gold prices, including inflation expectations, the U.S. dollar, uncertainty, and central-bank demand.

detail.abstract: Immigrants often encounter public information as a fragmented set of websites, forms, notices, call centers, and referrals. Access depends on more than the availability of a translated page. A person must identify a trustworthy source, understand the instruction, connect it to a personal situation, complete a digital or administrative task, and know where to seek qualified help when the issue exceeds ordinary information support. This article examines the role of public libraries in that pathway. It uses a structured qualitative review of scholarship, federal guidance, professional standards, and documented library practices available through 15 September 2026. The analysis treats the library as a local information institution rather than as a substitute for government, legal counsel, health care, or social services. It develops a five-stage library mediation model: reach, recognition, interpretation, navigation, and completion. The model shows how library collections, multilingual staff, public computers, digital-literacy instruction, community partnerships, and referral protocols can reduce information loss between official publication and practical use. The article also identifies limits. Libraries face uneven funding, staff capacity, language coverage, privacy risks, and pressure to handle questions outside professional scope. Effective programs therefore require explicit boundaries, recurring partnerships, source-verification rules, privacy safeguards, and outcome measures that extend beyond attendance. The central conclusion is that public libraries can serve as trusted access nodes within a broader public-information infrastructure. Their contribution is strongest when agencies design them into service delivery, maintain current multilingual materials, provide direct escalation channels, and accept responsibility for the accuracy and completion of public tasks.

detail.abstract: The contemporary business landscape is undergoing radical economic, technological, and cognitive shifts, forcing organizations to move beyond traditional management models. Knowledge management has emerged as a critical paradigm for creating, storing, transferring, and applying organizational knowledge to enhance competitiveness. The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence-through machine learning, natural language processing, and neural networks-offers unprecedented tools for analyzing data, uncovering patterns, and supporting intelligent decisionmaking, thereby fundamentally improving knowledge acquisition, organization, distribution, and application. In the Syrian context, organizations face exceptional challenges stemming from prolonged crisis, including destroyed infrastructure, brain drain, and weakened competitiveness. During the current recovery and reconstruction phase, there is an urgent need to develop organizational performance. AI-supported knowledge management represents a strategic entry point to manage institutional knowledge, improve decisions, and foster innovation. However, Arabic research on the integrative relationship between AI, knowledge management, and organizational performance remains scarce, with most Arab organizations still in early adoption stages. This study explores the relationship between AI-empowered knowledge management and organizational performance in Syrian organizations, providing an evidence-based forward-looking vision on harnessing this approach for institutional development. Given Syria's exceptional circumstances, AI-driven digital transformation could accelerate economic and developmental recovery if strategically deployed across sectors.

detail.abstract: Why do governments fail to restrain non-state violence when they can? Existing accounts emphasize weak capacity, direct state organization of violence, or strategic relationships with armed groups. They say less about decentralized violence enabled through enforcement choices. I develop a theory of institutional forbearance: governments may relax enforcement when violence advances goals they value, and anticipated leniency weakens deterrence. I test the argument in the West Bank, where radical settlers pursue territorial objectives partly shared by members of the Israeli government. Trump's election in November 2016 marked a reversal in the U.S. stance on the West Bank that unfolded in steps, from the inauguration to the recognition of Jerusalem as Israel's capital in December 2017, lowering the external cost of forbearance. Using difference-indifferences , I compare changes across locations differing in pre-Trump suitability for settlement expansion. Settler violence against Palestinians rises disproportionately in high-suitability locations, in stages that follow the sequence of signals, with the main break in January 2018, and remains elevated through 2023. The pattern is consistent with institutional forbearance: selective enforcement enables non-state violence without centralized direction or an explicit agreement.

detail.abstract: In 2010, Liberia received US$4.6 billion in debt cancellation under the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries (HIPC) Initiative and Multilateral Debt Relief Initiative of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank. Liberia's debt cancellation represented the largest extended to a single Sub-Saharan African country since the inception of the HIPC Initiative in 1996. Fifteen years later, public debt stands at US$2.63 billion, equivalent to 57.2 percent of GDP at end-2024. Both the IMF and World Bank now rate Liberia at high risk of overall public debt distress. This paper seeks to answer the central research question: How has Liberia's debt profile evolved in recent years, and what are the implications for its economic stability and policy interventions? To address this, the study traces the process of debt re-accumulation, breaks down the current debt portfolio into external and domestic components, analyzes the findings of the latest Joint Debt Sustainability Analysis, and examines the structure and initial outcomes of the 2024 IMF Extended Credit Facility programme. Drawing on multiple reports and studies, including the IMF Article IV and programme documents, World Bank/IMF Debt Sustainability Analyses, various debt management reports of the Government of Liberia, and the crosscountry debt relapse and fiscal dominance literatures, this study finds that Liberia's post-HIPC debt accumulation was driven by three reinforcing factors: new borrowing for legitimate infrastructure investment, a sequence of exogenous shocks, and a structural reliance on Central Bank of Liberia financing. Taken together, these factors trace a pattern of fiscal dominance consistent with what has been documented elsewhere in Sub-Saharan Africa. The domestic debt channel, in addition to external borrowing, is also identified as a principal driver of the deterioration in overall debt sustainability indicators, particularly the rising debt-to-GDP ratio and increasing debt service costs. The paper concludes that program-based fiscal consolidation, while showing genuine early results, is insufficient on its own; consistent with the fiscal dominance and debt relapse literatures, durable debt sustainability requires that borrowing constraints and central bank governance reforms be codified in domestic law rather than left to expire with the current Fund arrangement.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Feasibility Gap, the first doctrine under the Execution Architecture within the Execution Economics Canon of the VitroScript Working Paper Series. The doctrine explains the persistent divergence between announced or approved investment commitments and the capital, projects, and employment ultimately realised. The paper argues that this divergence should not automatically be interpreted as a shortage of finance or investor interest. Instead, it may reflect a distinct institutional gap between commitment and execution, where technical preparation, regulatory approvals, environmental and engineering assessments, financial structuring, permitting, organisational capacity, and project readiness must converge before an investment can become executable and finance-ready. The concept is examined through three country cases: South Africa's national investment conference pledges, Cameroon's approved investment portfolio under its investment incentive regime, and Nigeria's investment commitments and subsequent foreign direct investment flows. Together, these cases illustrate different forms of divergence between headline commitments and realised investment while also demonstrating why such divergence requires careful interpretation. The paper distinguishes genuine feasibility failure from the normal maturation period of large-scale investments and proposes falsifiable hypotheses for testing the mechanisms underlying the gap. It contributes to the emerging field of Execution Economics by shifting analytical attention from the volume of investment commitments mobilised toward the institutional processes that determine whether commitments are converted into measurable economic outcomes.

detail.abstract:
Lexicographic preferences are a foundational concept in choice theory and mathematical
economics. By violating continuity while preserving completeness and transitivity, they serve
as the canonical counterexample to the existence of a real-valued utility representation (Debreu,
1954); in particular, no continuous representation exists either. They have inspired five decades
of interdisciplinary research. This survey extends Fishburn’s (1974) foundational survey in three
directions: (i) theoretical developments including Chipman’s vector representation, lexicographic
probability systems, and non-standard equilibrium analysis; (ii) empirical testing methodologies,
including stated preference methods, latent class and latent cutoff models, attribute non-attendance,
and formal econometric identification challenges; and (iii) a synthesis of mathematical, game-theoretic,
and empirical literatures. Detailed proofs are provided for central theorems, with proof sketches for
non-standard and computational extensions. Applications are surveyed across economics, psychology,
computer science, health economics, and AI alignment, with particular attention to LP-trees and
multi-objective optimization. The survey concludes with prioritized open questions on empirical
identification, welfare, and computation.

detail.abstract: Shannon mutual information assigns a scalar quantity to an information structure, but a fixed quantity can be distributed across posterior beliefs in many ways. This paper studies the complete range of decision values attainable at an exact information quantity. In a finite Bayesian decision problem, an information configuration is represented by a Bayes-plausible distribution of posterior beliefs. For every quantity 𝑞, we define the exact-information value set 𝒱(𝑞), its upper and lower envelopes 𝐹 ! (𝑞) and 𝐹 " (𝑞), and the configuration-value dispersion 𝛥(𝑞) = 𝐹 ! (𝑞)-𝐹 " (𝑞). We show that 𝒱(𝑞) is a compact interval, that both endpoints are attained by configurations supported on at most 𝑛 + 1 posteriors, that 𝐹 ! is concave and nondecreasing, and that 𝐹 " is convex and nondecreasing. Consequently, 𝛥 is concave and vanishes at zero and full information. This produces a global dichotomy: dispersion is either identically zero or strictly positive at every interior information quantity. We then characterize the two cases. With finitely many actions and a full-support prior, dispersion is identically zero if and only if a single action is optimal in every state. Thus, whenever full revelation is valuable, equal Shannon information permits different decision values at every interior quantity. An eight-state example illustrates the result and shows that the ranking of equal-quantity configurations can reverse when the decision problem changes.

detail.abstract: Taiwan's relations with Hong Kong and Macao are highly complex, yet poorly understood by many foreigners. This is because, while Taiwan officially rejects the "One Country, Two Systems" model that is implemented in both cities, it also undeniably treats Hong Kong and Macao with a higher degree of closeness and cooperation than it treats the Mainland. The reverse is also true: the Mainland refuses to permit any level of official representation or presence from the Taiwan government in Mainland territory, but in Hong Kong and Macao, Taiwan has been able to operate a semi-official "embassy" without significant interference. Even as cross-strait ties have worsened in recent years, Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macao all appear committed to maintaining at least a minimum of contacts between the regions. This article explains the history of such relations and summarizes why Taiwan still treats the two cities differently from China and the rest of the world even as it tries to emphasize its unique "non-Chinese" identity to foreign audiences.

detail.abstract:
Background: Accurate interpretation of gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy is essential for diagnosing and monitoring inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), yet remains highly subjective due to clinician variability and subtle mucosal changes. Deep learning offers a path toward more objective assessment, but the comparative performance of modern CNN and transformer architectures in data‑limited clinical settings is not well established.

Methods: To address this gap, we introduce a controlled benchmark to evaluate 8 DL models on 960 expert-annotated images from the publicly available Kvasir dataset. The dataset covers eight clinically relevant GI classes, including ulcerative colitis, esophagitis, polyps, and anatomical landmarks, and was collected using endoscopic equipment at Vestre Viken Health Trust in Norway, consisting of four hospitals serving a population of 470,000. All models were trained under identical preprocessing, augmentation, and transfer‑learning conditions to ensure a fair and clinically meaningful comparison.

Findings: The modern CNNs outperform transformer‑based models under realistic data constraints typical of medical imaging. ConvNeXt-Tiny achieved the best overall performance, with 92.5% accuracy. ViT-B/16 and Swin-T had lower accuracy and much higher computational cost. Stability analysis across repeated runs further revealed that CNN‑based architectures exhibit lower variance and more reproducible behaviour, an essential requirement for clinical deployment. We additionally evaluated multiple ensemble methods, demonstrating their potential to further enhance predictive reliability.

Interpretation: CNNs still represent the most reliable option for GI endoscopy classification, with higher accuracy and stability than transformer models. Ensemble methods also increase robustness and allow the development of reliable AI-aided systems for IBD diagnosis and monitoring.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether the estimated effects of oil supply news shocks on U.S. inflation depend on how real economic activity is measured. We develop a Bayesian Proxy Mixed-Frequency Time-Varying Parameter Stochastic Volatility VAR that combines monthly oil-market and inflation variables with quarterly OECD and U.S. GDP. Using data from 1981--2025, we identify oil supply news shocks using crude-oil futures-price surprises around OPEC announcements and compare the GDP-based mixed-frequency model with a conventional monthly specification based on industrial production. A shock normalized to increase the real price of oil by 10\% raises U.S. inflation by approximately 0.67 percentage points on impact. Although the contemporaneous inflation response is relatively stable over time, its persistence varies substantially, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia--Ukraine war. The GDP- and industrial-production-based models generate nearly identical impact responses but diverge materially at subsequent horizons. Relative to the monthly model, the GDP-based specification produces cumulative inflation responses that are 1.26 percentage points larger after 12 months and 1.79 percentage points larger after 24 months. The models also imply substantial differences in the contribution of oil supply news shocks to inflation variability, with the COVID-19 episode representing a notable exception. Instrument diagnostics indicate that the oil supply news proxy is strongly relevant and provide no statistical evidence against the identifying restrictions. Overall, the results show that both time variation and the measurement and sampling frequency of real economic activity matter for structural inference about the inflationary effects of oil-market news.

title: Is there a Link between Hours Worked and Pressure on the Environment? Cross-Country Evidence from Europe
affiliations: European Trade Union Institute (ETUI)

detail.title: Is there a Link between Hours Worked and Pressure on the Environment? Cross-Country Evidence from Europe

publicationDetails.journalName: European Trade Union Institute (ETUI) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
The accelerating climate emergency and deepening ecological degradation require not only rapid decarbonisation but also structural changes to the way economies organise production and consumption. While most policy strategies have focused on substituting fossil fuels with renewable energy, there is mounting evidence to suggest that technological transition alone may be insufficient to achieve net-zero targets within planetary boundaries. Given that economic activity is embedded within broader social and ecological systems, with intrinsic linkages between labour markets and the environment (Ostrom 2009), meaningful climate mitigation will also demand measures beyond the energy sector – including those related to labour markets and the organisation of working time.

A growing body of research highlights the potential role of working time reduction as a complementary climate mitigation instrument. The core premise is that long working hours are associated with higher production, income and consumption levels which, in turn, put further pressure on the environment by driving energy use and the emission of greenhouse gases. Lower working time could reduce such pressure through multiple channels, among others by encouraging less carbon-intensive lifestyles including through reduced commuting or the establishment of sustainable consumption patterns. At the same time, shorter working hours are shown to be associated with improvements in wellbeing (Lepinteur 2019), potentially aligning social and environmental objectives.

Using data from 30 European countries1 over recent decades, this Technical Brief provides a brief empirical assessment of the relationship between hours worked and several environmental indicators, including carbon dioxide emissions (CO2), carbon or ecological footprints and energy use. The key empirical findings indicate a stable and significant positive association between the two. In other words, countries with longer average working hours tend to exhibit higher environmental strain, even when holding key structural features constant and accounting for sectoral composition, energy intensity and renewable energy shares across the countries under study. However, the results also show that a country’s energy mix, industrial structure and productivity patterns strongly influence the environmental pressures to which it is subject. This suggests that working time reforms must be integrated into comprehensive structural and energy transition policies if meaningful results are to be achieved.

The next section provides a brief background to the emerging research on working hours and the environment. The following two sections provide empirical analysis, consisting of a descriptive part followed by analytical findings based on a macro-econometric estimation framework which extends existing studies with a more fine-tuned methodological approach. The last section provides concluding remarks and directions for further research.

title: Paying for Reserve Capacity in ERCOT
affiliations: Rice University - Department of Economics, Rice University, Rice University and Rice University

detail.title: Paying for Reserve Capacity in ERCOT
detail.abstract: System operators require reserve capacity to accommodate load surges, equipment failures, and other unexpected events. To compensate firms for providing it, ERCOT has relied mainly on ancillary services (AS) payments. Since 2014, qualified generators supplying operating reserves when they are deemed to be scarce have earned additional payments calculated using an Operating Reserve Demand Curve (ORDC). In December 2025, these two mechanisms were combined to form AS demand curves, which were then incorporated into a real-time co-optimization (RTC) that simultaneously determines energy and AS quantities and prices. A major motivation for implementing RTC was to make reserve-capacity payments more responsive to current network conditions. However, ERCOT uses outdated, averaged data to derive its AS demand curves. We propose an alternative that yields AS demand curves that more accurately reflect the prevailing system state. We substitute measurements of network conditions in one SCED into an ARMA-ARCH model to calculate an ORDC and, thence, AS demand curves for the following SCED. We illustrate our method by applying it to SCED-interval data from 2023–2025. Although our application uses static AS supply curves as submitted by bidders, our alternative AS demand curves could instead be used with dynamic AS supply curves in an RTC.

title: Sequential Social Learning with Heterogeneous Inferential Biases

detail.abstract: We study sequential social learning when individuals receive private signals and observe the frequency of earlier choices. Agents use this frequency as a social prior but differ in its weight and may misperceive private-signal precision. We show that this heterogeneity can be summarized by behavioral thresholds: the majority required for social information to outweigh a conflicting private signal. The threshold distribution is sufficient for aggregate dynamics, determining the probability of the next action at every action share. We establish convergence and characterize stable long-run outcomes. Strong social responses favor extreme outcomes, whereas sufficient reliance on private information can sustain informative interior outcomes. Multimodality can generate multiple stable interior outcomes, while unimodality sharply restricts their number and location; average behavior is generally insufficient. Because thresholds can be elicited independently, the model generates out-of-sample predictions for finite-horizon dynamics, long-run outcomes, and comparative statics, linking individual inference to collective learning.

detail.abstract: Our study was a return to the Maltese Annual Notifiable Infectious Disease Reports: 2010-2024 (Maltese DataBase) to revisit the gaps, voids, and misclassification flaws we encountered with our initial examination of the Maltese DataBase, focusing on the stats (incidents and deaths) associated with Legionnaires' Disease, a respiratory condition. Specifically, we sought to rewrite our initial examination of the Maltese DataBase and to recalibrate our initial determination (IBM/SPSS) of the potential (current and emerging) impact of Legionnaires' Disease on the public health of the Maltese population. Latent and foreboding trends in the Maltese DataBase were unchanged, remaining worrisome. Our initial determination (with Central Limit Theory) yielded a Maltese Chance of Death at 3.9%-12.4% from Legionnaires' Disease, covering an initial sample of 160 incidents and 13 deaths during 2010-2022. Revisiting the Maltese DataBase with acute curiosity, we began a systematic review by reclarifying content and retracking, reverifying, and unraveling data to reassure validity and accuracy of our initial study, plus the consistency of posted incidents and deaths. We repeated our IBM/SPSS/Central Limit Theory analysis using new data to reassure the integrity and validity of our research. Recalibration revealed an updated Chance of Death at 1.83%-11.1%, using a sample set of 108 incidents and 7 deaths during 2010-2022. We present, also, suggestions for improving the management, standardization, and auditing of the Maltese Annual Notifiable Infectious Disease Reports-which is a vital resource for promoting awareness and readiness, essential for the future of Malta. A strategic step is to consider adopting and installing an AI tool to manage and operate the Maltese Database.

title: When Energy becomes a Weapon: Can International Law Really Prevent Energy from being used as a Tool of Political Power?
affiliations: Fountain University

detail.title: When Energy becomes a Weapon: Can International Law Really Prevent Energy from being used as a Tool of Political Power?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no financial, personal, professional, or other relationships that could have influenced, or could reasonably be perceived to have influenced, the research or preparation of this article.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant or financial support from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Energy has quietly become one of the sharpest tools of political pressure available to states, from the 1973 OPEC oil embargo to Russia's manipulation of gas flows to Europe and the still-unresolved sabotage of the Nord Stream pipelines. This article asks a direct question: can international law actually stop energy from being turned into a political weapon? Rather than treating this as a matter of abstract doctrine, it traces the practical legal tools already in place;  the principle that states control their own natural resources, the customary rule against coercing other states, the World Trade Organization's security exception, the investment protections built into the Energy Charter Treaty, the law governing sanctions and countermeasures, and the rules that apply when energy infrastructure itself is attacked. It argues that these tools genuinely constrain the most extreme forms of energy coercion, but were never designed, individually or together, to close the field entirely. Self-judging security exceptions, a narrow customary rule on economic coercion, the fragmentation of investment law following Europe's retreat from the Energy Charter Treaty, and the practical immunity of powerful states from binding enforcement all leave real gaps. The article concludes that international law narrows, without eliminating, the space in which energy can be converted into political leverage, and that closing that space further will depend as much on sharper legal interpretation and reduced dependency as on any single new treaty.

detail.title: Repo Rate Dynamics
detail.abstract: This paper analyses U.S. secured repo spreads by jointly looking into reserves, dealer balance-sheet usage, hedge fund leverage, and Treasury issuance. Using a quantile regression framework, the results show that repo market dynamics are strongly state-dependent. Higher level of reserves consistently compress repo spreads to the Federal Reserve’s overninght reverse repo offering rate and remain the primary stabilizing force, particularly in tighter funding conditions. Hedge fund activity appears to amplify dealer balance-sheet pressures in lower quantiles, reflecting the impact of leveraged demand in normal markets. As spreads rise, this effect weakens. Instead, heavier Treasury issuance appears to weigh on repo spreads via its stronger effect on dealer balance sheet pressures. Overall, U.S. repo spreads are affected by the supply of central bank liquidity,  demand for leverage, Treasury issuance and intermediary capacity. Crucially, these drivers are not equally relevant across the distribution of funding conditions.

detail.abstract: This paper studies narrative exhaustion as a state transition rather than a directional trading signal. Using Market Prism's proprietary point-in-time equity panel, we examine high-confidence exhaustion episodes from the live measurement period beginning March 2, 2026 and condition subsequent returns on fair-value divergence, narrative verdict transitions, narrative-energy trajectories, and thematic context. After de-duplicating consecutive exhausted observations into distinct episodes, deeply undervalued securities (fair-value divergence below-20%) exhibit positive subsequent drift: across 196 episodes, mean returns are +1.74% at five trading days, +3.04% at ten days, and +2.54% at twenty days; the twenty-day median is +2.88% and 60.4% of observations are positive. Marginal undervaluation does not display the same behavior. On the overvalued side, exhaustion alone is not bearish. A narrower state characterized by persistent narrative risk and collapsing narrative energy produces a-1.39% mean and-1.83% median twenty-day return across 58 de-duplicated episodes; the SPY-adjusted mean and median are-1.53% and-2.66%, respectively. In the later live measurement period, the same state records a-3.90% mean and-3.64% median twenty-day return while other overvalued exhaustion states remain positive. Among undervalued securities in the later measurement period, transitions from an exhausted narrative toward renewed structural support or accumulation are associated with +6.59% mean, +5.42% median, and +5.39% SPY-relative twenty-day returns (n = 25), though this subgroup is exploratory. The evidence supports a conditional interpretation: exhaustion marks depletion of an informational state, while subsequent direction depends on valuation displacement and whether narrative structure deteriorates, persists, or reconstructs.

title: Aggregate Gains from AI and Their Distribution: Global Evidence from Usage Data

detail.title: Aggregate Gains from AI and Their Distribution: Global Evidence from Usage Data
detail.abstract: How large is the labor cost saved by AI, and how is it distributed across occupations? Using five waves of the Anthropic Economic Index (January 2025 to February 2026), we construct two novel measures from observed AI usage across countries over the world. The AI concentration index (ACI) shows that in developing economies, virtually all AI usage-based value is generated in a small professional enclave (ACI near 1.0); high-income economies average 0.4 to 0.5, with concentration declining in many countries. The labor cost equivalent (LCE) values the time currently saved by AI at $2.7 trillion annually (3.4% of GDP), an indicative measure of the labor cost of that time. Income and regulatory readiness predict concentration; lacking an official English language slows broadening, a barrier for developing countries.

title: What Drives Crypto Mining? Evidence from Hardware Imports

detail.title: What Drives Crypto Mining? Evidence from Hardware Imports
detail.abstract: Understanding financial activity beyond traditional regulatory frameworks is essential for policymakers. Yet cryptocurrency mining—which offers a direct entry point into the crypto ecosystem without relying on traditional financial intermediaries—remains highly opaque. We propose a novel measurement approach using detailed customs data that tracks exports of crypto mining hardware from the world’s dominant producers. This trade-based proxy allows us to analyze the global distribution of mining hardware imports and identify their key drivers, guided by a stylized model. Empirically, mining surges respond strongly to global factors such as cryptocurrency prices and hardware costs, while domestic factors—including electricity prices and ambient temperature—shape the cross-country distribution of activity. Our findings highlight how global crypto markets, natural endowments, and policy choices jointly influence mining incentives, offering valuable insights for policymakers concerned with financial stability risks and energy subsidy misuse.

title: Industrial Policy and Supply Chain Bottlenecks in Commodity Markets: Evidence from Rare Earth Elements

detail.title: Industrial Policy and Supply Chain Bottlenecks in Commodity Markets: Evidence from Rare Earth Elements
detail.abstract: Recent supply shortages have intensified concerns about supply chain bottlenecks, prompting policymakers to adopt industrial policies to promote reshoring and import diversification. Rare earth element (REE) markets, where supply chains are highly concentrated across stages, particularly for refining, is a clear example. This paper quantifies the costs of de-risking supply chains using a dynamic global trade model calibrated with detailed market, industry andgeological data. In the model, upstream (mining) and downstream (refining) production is slow-moving and determined by investment in capacity (CAPEX). To illustrate the model’s properties, we evaluate how different policies can decrease downstream REE exposure from any single supplier by comparing CAPEX subsidies and stylized revenue-support policies under unilateral and simultaneous action among various importers. De-risking supply chains through targeted industrial policies is fiscally costly, although less so if pursued simultaneously by various importers. The fiscal cost of downstream unilateral CAPEX subsidies, for example, drops from 134% of the annual U.S. REE market (about 1.13 billion dollars) by 2035, to 90% under simultaneous action by other REE importers. Of course, de-escalation of trade tensions remains the first-best outcome.

title: What Explains Timely Repayments to the IMF? The Roles of Policy Reforms and Borrower Fundamentals

detail.title: What Explains Timely Repayments to the IMF? The Roles of Policy Reforms and Borrower Fundamentals
detail.abstract: IMF borrowers have demonstrated a very strong track record of timely repayments to the IMF since the 1990s—indeed, no new episodes of protracted overdue financial obligations (OFOs) have occurred since 2001. This represents a marked improvement from the experience of the 1980s and early 1990s. Through quantitative modeling we find that countries’ international reserves coverage of debt service due to the IMF and other creditors, external debt levels, macroeconomic conditions, and broad institutional strength played key roles in distinguishing between past cases with timely repayments and those with protracted arrears. However, we also find that policy reforms and changes in other qualitative factors since the 1990s weakened the relationship between quantitative indicators of repayment capacity and the likelihood of protracted arrears episodes. While stronger macroeconomic and institutional fundamentals of borrowers have contributed to greater timeliness of repayments, a large portion of the improvement remains unexplained by country-specific factors. The timing of this improvement is consistent with implementation of a cooperative strategy on OFOs and other policies that have incentivized cooperation and mitigated “residual” risks on IMF lending relative to the underlying fundamentals of borrowers.

title: Optimal Monetary Policy Rules: The Polish Case

detail.title: Optimal Monetary Policy Rules: The Polish Case

detail.abstract: Could monetary policy have prevented the 2021-2023 inflation spike? To what degree monetary policy should react to supply shocks? We answer these questions by evaluating eleven monetary policy strategies and deriving optimal Taylor rules in an estimated quarterly macroeconometric model of the Polish economy, using a full general-equilibrium historical counterfactual for 2008Q1-2026Q2 and a stochastic simulation over 2026Q3-2055Q4. We find that 1) NBP's monetary policy is beaten by most considered rules due to overly accommodative policy during the 2016-2019 expansion and the 2021-2023 inflation shock; 2) due to weak impact of interest rates on inflation, no strategy that keeps interest rates within historically reasonable bounds would have materially reduced inflation relative to the observed 2022 peak. Cutting inflation by a third would have required a policy rate above 80%; 3) forward-looking information matters-forward-looking Taylor rules tend to perform well under all setups due to relatively low output and interest rate volatility, despite somewhat higher inflation volatility relative to contemporaneous rules. 4) Preference for interest rate stability not only introduces inertia but also reduces responsiveness to non-core inflation. If only inflation and output gap stability matter, an aggressive Taylor rule based on headline inflation is optimal, implying strong response to supply shocks. Once policy rate stability is considered, more moderate, inertial and core inflation-based Taylor rules are preferred as lower interest rate volatility outweighs somewhat higher inflation volatility, implying weaker-but non-zero-response to supply shocks. 5) Strict inflation-forecast targeting delivers inflation significantly closer to target at a cost of a substantially more volatile output and unrealistically high volatility in interest rates.

title: Macroeconomic Effects of Rare Earths Supply Chain Disruptions

detail.title: Macroeconomic Effects of Rare Earths Supply Chain Disruptions
detail.abstract: Rare earth elements (REEs) are critical inputs in high‑tech manufacturing. Following China’s 2025 export licensing requirements on REEs and permanent magnets, concerns have risen about the macroeconomic consequences of supply disruptions in import‑dependent economies. Standard assessments based on “value added at risk” (VAAR) ignore production network linkages and input reallocation. We develop a small open economy model with imported REEs and production networks, calibrated using an REE‑augmented input–output table from USGS data. Applying the model to the United States, Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Japan, and India, we find substantial cross‑country heterogeneity in response to an 80% reduction in REEs supply. The most exposed economies are Japan, U.S. and Germany. Under low substitution elasticities (horizons under one year), these economies experience a GDP loss of 1.8, 1.5, and 1.2 percent, respectively. These differences reflect heterogeneity in sectoral composition, factor shares, and the strength of forward linkages of REE-intensive sectors. Under higher elasticities (longer horizons), aggregate losses become negligible.

detail.abstract: Corporate carbon-neutral commitments create a measurement problem for investors because the activities that reduce valuechain emissions do not map cleanly onto separately disclosed financial-statement line items. This study asks how much of the cost of Apple Inc.'s 2030 carbon-neutral transition an external investor can observe. It combines Apple's Environmental Progress Reports, Green Bond impact reports, supplier disclosures and SEC filings with U.S. CPI data, official 2025 EU and UK emissions-trading prices and ECB exchange rates. The analysis distinguishes identifiable climate-related allocation, Apple corporate expenditure and the incremental economic cost of Apple 2030. Apple's reported gross carbon footprint fell from 38.4 MtCO2e in FY2015 to 15.3 MtCO2e in FY2025, a 60.2% decline, while CPI-adjusted revenue rose 31.1%; gross emissions intensity relative to real revenue fell 69.6%. Yet the FY2025 Form 10-K does not separately identify a comprehensive Apple 2030 cost. The 2019 Green Bond provides more granular voluntary disclosure: $1.5961 billion had been cumulatively allocated by FY2025 against 39 million Apple-reported projected lifetime tonnes of emissions mitigated or offset, implying a green-bond allocation intensity of $40.93 per projected lifetime tonne. This ratio is not a marginal abatement cost because the allocation can include contractual NPVs and investments and excludes project financial returns. FY2025 allocation of $532 million equalled 0.128% of revenue and 0.539% of research-defined free cash flow. Supplier disclosures show substantial physical decarbonisation activity, but neither supplier expenditure nor ultimate economic incidence is publicly recoverable. The evidence therefore supports an accounting-visibility result rather than a single estimate of the economic cost of Apple 2030.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates structural gender differences in belief formation and self persuasion by exploiting randomized position assignments in competitive debate tournaments. While both genders initially shift their factual beliefs to align with their assigned proposition, we document a stark divergence in how they respond to persuasion goals. Male debaters systematically inflate their unverified confidence to signal authority. In contrast, female debaters, facing asymmetric reputational costs for unjustified confidence, heavily discount this confidence premium and instead exhibit profound, post-debate factual entrenchment. This behavioral gap is powerfully amplified by pre-existing ideological alignment, which triggers an extreme confidence "echo chamber" in men and severe factual polarization in women. These divergent responses persist regardless of prior debate experience, competitive achievements, or financial incentives for accuracy. Ultimately, the findings demonstrate that men and women utilize fundamentally different psychological channels of strategic self-deception and cognitive dissonance resolution when navigating competitive environments.

detail.title: Four Foundational Laws in the Ontology of Representational Money

detail.abstract: Conventional monetary theory tends to examine money through its functions—as a medium of exchange, unit of account, and store of value—while giving less attention to the ontological conditions that allow a monetary claim to exist and remain functional within an institutional system. This paper proposes that representational money should not be understood primarily as a physical object or numerical quantity, but as an institutional claim sustained by trust, recorded through representation, and governed by an ordered system of rights and obligations. The paper develops four foundational laws: 1. The Law of Trust — the inner principal that gives monetary representation its social acceptance; 2. The Balance Law — the requirement that claims and obligations remain institutionally accountable; 3. The Ordered Law — the requirement that rights, obligations, payment, and delivery exist within a coherent institutional order; and 4. The Sequence Law — the requirement that monetary states and transactions remain temporally ordered and historically traceable. These laws are presented not as physical laws, but as ontological conditions of institutional monetary existence. The framework further distinguishes commodity-referenced money from sovereign fiat money. Gold, for example, possesses physical scarcity and value independent of the continued existence of a particular sovereign, whereas fiat money ultimately depends upon the continuity, credibility, and acceptance of the institutional order that recognizes it. Treasury securities may constitute assets for holders and liabilities for the sovereign, but they do not constitute the ultimate guarantor of fiat money; the sovereign and the institutional order remain the deeper source of monetary validity. The paper uses the transition from Soviet ruble systems to successor monetary regimes and the thought experiment of Monopoly money to illustrate a central proposition: A monetary token does not become money merely because it exists physically or numerically; it becomes money because an institutional order continues to recognize and accept the claim it represents. When the representation remains in a ledger while its underlying institutional capacity to command purchasing power collapses, the result may be described as Considered Being: formally existent, but substantively impaired in its economic function.

detail.abstract: This essay presents a theoretical framework for understanding the persistence and rupture of social systems, rooted in the biological and psychological logic of the survival instinct. It argues that individual conformity and collective inertia are emergent products of adaptive responses to complex environments, operating on both a somatic and an ontological register (Giddens, 1991), and identifies three evolutionary phases of stabilization-instinctual, organizational, and ideological-through which this adaptation accumulates. The essay's central claim is that the same survival impulse, when inverted by systemic failure, becomes the engine of destabilization: a "survival flip" that is not a mechanistic threshold but a dynamic struggle moderated by the collectively negotiated perception of injustice and resolved, at the population level, through threshold cascades of collective action (Granovetter, 1978; Kuran, 1991). Building on this, the essay argues that the most effective point of intervention is a paradigm shift: a single leverage point that simultaneously accelerates collapse, by undermining the old system's ideological legitimacy, and guides reconstruction, by supplying a coherent framework for what follows. The argument is positioned against relative-deprivation accounts of rebellion (Gurr, 1970), the collective-action problem (Olson, 1965), and structural theories of revolution (Skocpol, 1979; Goldstone, 1991), and draws on complex adaptive systems theory (Holland, 1995; Meadows, 1999) and the social psychology of radical change (Moghaddam, 2018, 2024) to bring psychology, systems theory, and political economy into a single interpretive lens.

title: Understanding the Implications of Outsourced Laboratory and Radiology Diagnostic Services on Public Financial Management in Zanzibar

detail.title: Understanding the Implications of Outsourced Laboratory and Radiology Diagnostic Services on Public Financial Management in Zanzibar
detail.abstract: Background: Outsourcing has emerged as a strategic approach to address technical and financial constraints in healthcare diagnostics in low-resource settings. In Zanzibar, laboratory and radiology services were outsourced to private providers to improve efficiency and accessibility. However, systematic evidence on the model's impact on financial governance and equitable service delivery remains scarce. This study aimed to understand the impact of outsourcing on the allocative efficiency of laboratory and radiology diagnostic services in Zanzibar. Methods: We conducted a convergent parallel mixed-methods study, theoretically grounded in Principal-Agent Theory and operationalized through the Public Expenditure Tracking Survey (PETS) methodology. The study was performed across four purposively selected public hospitals in Zanzibar, stratified by geography (Unguja/Pemba) and location (urban/rural). We collected quantitative data for one fiscal year before (2021-2022) and after (2023-2024) the outsourcing intervention. Primary outcomes were the Allocative Efficiency Ratio (AER), financial leakage rates, and diagnostic test volumes. Quantitative analysis involved descriptive statistics, paired ttests to assess within-facility changes, and independent t-tests to evaluate urban-rural disparities. Concurrently, we conducted 10 in-depth key informant interviews with Ministry of Health officials, hospital managers, and private providers. Qualitative data were analyzed using thematic analysis to explore operational and governance challenges. Results: Quantitative findings demonstrated a significant improvement in efficiency following outsourcing. The mean Allocative Efficiency Ratio (AER) increased from 61.5% to 77.4% (mean improvement 15.95%, 95% CI [6.40, 25.49], p=0.013), equating to a reduction in financial leakage from 38.5% to 22.6%. Aggregate diagnostic test volumes surged by 109.3% (p=0.032). However, a profound urban-rural equity gap was uncovered. Urban facilities achieved markedly superior post-intervention AERs (90% and 83%) and test volume growth (135.0% mean increase) compared to their rural counterparts (71% and 65% AER; 83.6% mean increase). Qualitative results elucidated the mechanisms behind this disparity, identifying three key systemic failures: (1) chronic delays in government reimbursements, creating liquidity crises for providers; (2) a onesize-fits-all per-test payment model that ignored the higher transaction costs in rural areas; and (3) fragmented oversight and weak contractual governance, which disproportionately hampered rural facility performance. Conclusion: Outsourcing of diagnostic services in Zanzibar significantly improved financial efficiency and service output, yet these benefits were unevenly distributed, exacerbating urbanrural disparities. To ensure outsourcing contributes to equitable healthcare, policymakers must prioritize financial accountability mechanisms and equitable contract design. Further research is needed to assess the long-term sustainability and quality of outsourced services.

detail.abstract: Accurate forecasting of equity market volatility is essential for risk management, portfolio allocation, and derivative pricing. From a machine learning and soft-computing perspective, this paper investigates the relative predictive role of idiosyncratic and systematic jump risks in forecasting realized volatility across major U.S. equity market sectors, considering both volatility levels and directional movements. We conduct a comprehensive out-of-sample comparison of linear benchmark models and a broad set of machine learning methods. The results show that selected machine-learning models improve forecasting accuracy relative to HAR, but the gains depend on the sector and algorithm, and HAR remains a competitive benchmark. Feature importance analysis indicates that systematic jump risk contributes more strongly to volatility predictability than idiosyncratic jump risk. To further capture nonlinear and timevarying market dynamics, we propose novel regime-dependent predictors derived from a Markov regimeswitching framework and incorporate them into the learning process. These regime-sensitive features lead to a marked improvement in forecasting performance, particularly for volatility direction prediction. Overall, the findings demonstrate that integrating jump-based feature engineering and regime-dependent information within machine learning frameworks yields more accurate and robust volatility forecasts.

detail.abstract: Measures of exposure to generative artificial intelligence are collected at three levels of the labour market: occupations, tasks, and skills, and compared as though they described one object. This paper conceptualises the labour market as one wage bill at three levels and counts what each can identify: 829 observed wages against an identity, against 17,383 task prices that no wage data can contradict, and against 25 skill prices that can. The testability of quantities in this literature follows from how many statements the Occupational Information Network’s analysts wrote at each level. Three findings emerge. The leading capability measures are one construct under three names: carrying the Eloundou task ratings to abilities reproduces the Felten ability scores in the right order across AI applications, the Srinivasan automation score is the Eloundou construction re-run on a later release, and augmentation is explained to 77 percent by a quadratic in automation. The skill layer supports a structure of about twenty-five dimensions, which explains occupational wages at a cross-validated 0.648 in the Network’s own named groups, with loadings that are usable as changes and not as levels. On a balanced panel of 693 occupations from 2012 to 2025, nothing in realised wages or employment has moved beyond ordinary volatility since language models were released: no skill group moved by more than 1.51 times its own year-to-year variation, and every deviation from the pre-2020 path begins with the pandemic.

detail.abstract: This study examines anti-danmei transmigration fiction, a genre written by Chinese radical feminists in which female protagonists enter danmei (Boys' Love) novels and refuse their scripted roles as marginalised female characters. Drawing on Sara Ahmed's feminist killjoy framework, extended through the concept of horizontal hostility, this study analyses two anti-danmei novels and their surrounding paratexts published on Jinjiang Literature City. Reflexive thematic analysis reveals three findings. First, the anti-danmei narrative functions as a feminist killjoy that exposes danmei's male-centredness as a happiness script sustaining female suffering. Second, the feminist snap from danmei produces horizontal hostility directed at danmei readers and LGBTQ communities, reclassifying both as complicit with patriarchy. Third, the killjoy survival kit operates through rage-based female solidarity and the strategic instrumentalisation of state power. This study argues that previous scholarship's framing of danmei through an empowerment/complicity binary cannot account for this phenomenon. Under authoritarian constraint, where the state compresses the space available for marginalised expression, feminist energy redirects horizontally. The feminist project consumes its potential allies before reaching the structures it set out to dismantle.
