detail.abstract:
Some technology companies in the United States have started to give their engineers budgets of AI tokens, and whether those budgets are part of compensation is already under debate. The practice has barely reached Mexico, but Mexican law already contains the rules that would govern it. This paper argues that the legal treatment of a token budget depends mainly on how freely the worker can use the tokens, and proposes a four-level scale. At the first level the tokens can only be used for work; they are a work tool and do not form part of salary. At the second the worker may use them for personal purposes, and they become an in-kind benefit that forms part of salary and taxable income. At the third, a balance that can be spent across several providers resembles a grocery voucher, although the favorable voucher regime probably does not reach it. At the fourth the tokens can be transferred and used as payment, and only then could they fit the definition of virtual asset in the Fintech Law, provided the budget is not denominated in currency. At no level are tokens money. The Constitution requires wages to be paid in legal tender, and the Fintech Law distinguishes virtual assets from it. detail.abstract: Canada's treatment of residential capital gains under the Income Tax Act's Principal Residence Exemption (PRE) offers an uncapped tax shelter with significant structural, economic, and distributional ramifications. While Canada and the United States share geographic proximity, cultural similarities, and fundamentally similar tax structures, their approaches to capital gains taxation on primary residences diverge significantly. Unlike the U.S. regime, which caps its capital gains exclusion at USD $250,000, Canada exempts the entire qualifying gain realized on the disposition of a principal residence, providing an uncapped tax shelter for residential real estate. This contrast extends to intergenerational wealth transfers: the United States imposes a unified estate-and-gift tax on very large fortunes, whereas Canada's absence of a separate estate or inheritance tax, combined with the unlimited PRE, allows substantial housing appreciation to pass between generations with comparatively little tax consequences. Because residential real estate is, by a wide margin, the largest single store of household wealth-with an aggregate value of global real estate vastly exceeding that of the global stock market-the PRE's preferential tax treatment has implications that extend far beyond foregone tax revenue and individual housing decisions. By offering an unlimited tax-free return on owner-occupied housing, the PRE actively distorts household portfolio choices, inflates housing demand, and alters economy-wide capital allocation. Furthermore, the PRE generates pronounced distributional distortions by serving as an uncapped, passive subsidy to existing property owners, the exemption deepens the wealth divide between homeowners and prospective buyers or renters. Concurrently, it incentivizes the construction and purchase of larger dwellings, expanding the environmental footprint of housing consumption. Ultimately, this comparative analysis reveals a central policy paradox: despite Canada's reputation as a progressive and redistributive welfare state, its uncapped Principal Residence Exemption and absence of a separate estate or inheritance tax create a less progressive framework than the corresponding U.S. regime.

detail.abstract: Oil-price volatility is often reported to transmit to financial systems episodically, in a few crisis windows, rather than continuously. detail.abstract:
Background: Same-person co-detection, population synchrony, and delayed ecological associations describe different aspects of respiratory-pathogen dependence but are often interpreted interchangeably. We compared these structures and assessed their environmental and geographical robustness.

Methods: This retrospective multilevel study included 73,404 children admitted with acute respiratory tract infection and tested with a uniform 11-pathogen panel in Fuzhou, China, between Sept 17, 2019, and Dec 31, 2025. We estimated adjusted same-person co-detection odds ratios (ORs), pre-whitened correlations of daily positivity, and quasi-binomial distributed lag models for temperature, air pollutants, and 110 ordered pathogen pairs. Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied. Prespecified findings were assessed in 34,607 children from five other cities.

Findings: A total of 73,404 children in Fuzhou participated in the testing, 7,551 (10.29%) had at least two pathogens detected. Fifty-one of 55 adjusted same-person associations were FDR significant: 50 were inverse and HBoV–HRV was positive (OR 1.38, 95% CI: 1.22–1.56). Thirteen inverse associations were consistent across all pandemic stages and all replicated externally. In the primary ± 21-day pre-whitened analysis, 20 pairs met q<0.01 and |rho|>0.10 and all were positive and most occurred at lag 0.   Environmental adjustment reduced the pathogen network to ten globally FDR-significant ordered associations. Two temperature associations and three fully adjusted pathogen associations, but no pollutant association, met strict external replication criteria.

Interpretation: Association patterns depended on analytical scale. Same-person co-detection was predominantly inverse, whereas population series showed synchrony. After environmental adjustment, most ordered associations lost significance or failed to replicate externally. Limited transportability of environmental and lagged associations argues against interpreting them as direct biological facilitation or interference.

detail.abstract: In May 2023, Nigeria's government abolished petroleum subsidy regime that had cost an estimated ₦4.39trn in 2022, triggering a 261.8% increase in prices and reigniting debate over reconciling fiscal consolidation with distributional equity in a subsidy-dependent, oilexporting economy. The findings show a reform that is fiscally sound and relatively progressive, yet povertyincreasing in absolute terms and inadequately compensated. The paper closes with recommendations on transfer scale, sequencing, and targeting, framed through an energy justice lens.

detail.abstract:
Background: Household shocks may impair child linear growth, but standard adjustment is biased when prior shocks change later wealth, food security, and growth.

Methods: We analysed Young Lives data from Ethiopia, India, Peru, and Vietnam (five rounds, 2002 to 2016; 7,126 children). Shock effects on final height-for-age z-score (HAZ) were estimated with cross-fitted g-methods (marginal structural model, g-computation, and longitudinal targeted maximum likelihood estimation) and a same-learner benchmark, with inverse-probability-of-censoring weighting for attrition.

Findings: Each additional shock-year lowered final HAZ (marginal structural model -0.107 SD, 95% CI -0.121 to -0.093), unchanged under full-cohort censoring weighting. The central finding was heterogeneity: the same measured exposure produced materially different effects, from -0.128 SD in Ethiopia to -0.029 SD in Vietnam (interval including the null); the difference between Vietnam and Ethiopia was 0.098 SD (95% CI 0.038 to 0.162, P < 0.001). Transportability analysis showed these differences were not explained by measured covariate composition.

Interpretations: A pooled shock effect is not transportable: the same measured shock produces significantly different effects across settings, for structural rather than compositional reasons. Shock vulnerability, and the evidence used to target it, should be treated as setting specific.

detail.abstract: Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in computer-aided diagnosis and clinical decision-making. However, most high-performance segmentation models rely on large parameter sizes and substantial computational costs, which limit their applicability in real-time inference and resource-constrained scenarios. To address the insufficient structural representation capability of lightweight models under weak boundaries, strong noise, and cross-modality conditions, this paper proposes an efficient hybrid lightweight medical image segmentation network, termed XHNet. The proposed approach introduces a feature-selective inverted-bottleneck convolution block to explicitly enhance the selection of critical structural features under lightweight constraints. In addition, a hierarchical encoder design combined with a multi-scale semantic selection mechanism is employed to improve structural sensitivity to true lesion regions and maintain semantic consistency across different feature levels. Extensive experiments conducted on nine public datasets covering four medical imaging modalities, including endoscopy, ultrasound, dermoscopy, and histopathology, demonstrate that XHNet achieves stable and competitive segmentation performance with only 0.53M parameters and 0.34 GFLOPs. In particular, the proposed model exhibits strong robustness in cross-data set evaluations and complex imaging conditions. Overall, the experimental results indicate that XHNet achieves a favorable balance between segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency, providing an effective solution for high-precision, low-cost real-time medical image segmentation.

detail.abstract: Option collars are designed to reduce equity downside, but retirement portfolios face a different objective: avoiding depletion while financing withdrawals. We ask whether lower conventional downside risk necessarily translates into lower retirement depletion risk. We closely replicate Milevsky and Posner (2014), then bridge from their theoretical collar model to Cboe option-strategy benchmark histories. In the 1986-2021 monthly benchmark sample, the Cboe S&P 500 95-110 Collar Index (CLL) materially reduces volatility and drawdowns and strongly outperforms S&P 500 total return (SPTR) during large negative months, yet repeatedly sacrifices return in positive months. At a 5% initial withdrawal rate over 20-year historical windows, CLL produces more depletion events than SPTR under both deterministic 2.5% inflation and historical CPI-U. Dependence-aware moving-block bootstrap experiments, however, reduce the estimated CLL-minus-SPTR depletion difference to only 0.00-0.61 percentage points across 6-36 month blocks. The evidence therefore does not support a general claim that collars increase depletion risk. It supports the narrower conclusion that successful downside hedging does not imply successful depletion hedging: crash protection competes with cumulative upside sacrifice, and retirement outcomes are sequence-dependent.

detail.abstract: I study labor markets in which firms both hire via referrals and are race blind or colorblind. I develop an employment model showing that despite initial equality in ability, employment, wages, and network structure, minorities receive disproportionately fewer jobs through referrals and lower expected wages, simply because their social group is smaller. detail.abstract: Strategic positioning models commonly assess firms within a comparatively stable frame of reference. The Schließmann Strategy Cube distinguishes three strategic coordinates: relative strength in the Strategically Relevant Market, performance in that market, and viability in the relevant system. This paper develops the cube into a dynamic strategic coordinate system in which both the organisation and its strategic frame of reference can change over time. Strategic state is represented as Q_t(C_t) = [S_t(C_t), P_t(C_t), V_t(C_t)], where C_t denotes the strategically relevant context at time t. The paper is an analytical and methodological contribution. It formalises context dependency, strategic movement, acceleration, context migration and recontextualisation, and it specifies a multi-level diagnostic architecture linking system variables and interdependencies to complexity, agility, robustness, viability and strategic position. Viability is represented as a system-specific function of agility, robustness and complexity. The heuristic relation V ~ (A•R)/K is used as a causal diagnostic logic and is explicitly not treated as a calibrated mathematical law or aggregate corporate score. The contribution is completed by a falsifiable longitudinal research architecture for Viability Trajectory Monitoring. It specifies how future studies can operationalise the three coordinates, observe ΔQ_t, distinguish firm movement from context migration, and test whether changes in systemic viability precede changes in conventional performance indicators. Seven research propositions are derived. The central claim is methodological: strategic diagnosis gains explanatory depth when it observes position, direction, dynamics and movement of the reference context within one coherent coordinate system. detail.abstract: This paper examines the regulatory design of artificial intelligence (AI) in Chile through the lens of adaptive regulation theory and dynamic risk governance. Using a comparative institutional analysis of five cases —the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, Singapore and the Chilean AI bill (consolidated Bills No. 16.821-19 and 15.869-19)—, with information current as of 16 December 2025, three design dimensions are ordinally coded: robustness of normative principles (P), technical translation capacity (T) and bureaucratic friction (F), combined in a heuristic regulatory effectiveness function E = (P × T) / F. Three findings emerge: (1) the cases converge on principles, and differences in expected effectiveness are driven by T and F; (2) in Chile, friction stems less from the AI law than from its overlap with four adjacent compliance regimes; and (3) technical translation capacity is the binding constraint of the Chilean design, since risk self-classification is only credible under ex post verification, and the text approved at first reading provides for infringements and fines but not for the authority, the procedure or the metrics needed to enforce them. Policy implications follow, in order of priority: enabling enforcement through an expressly empowered authority and procedure; equipping it with a technical risk taxonomy and verifiable metrics under online monitoring; and formalising inter-agency coordination, while retaining divergence from the European model in implementation mechanisms. detail.abstract: This study examines cross-cultural differences in implicit leadership schemas between Canadian organizational leaders (N = 38) and international Master's students preparing for leadership roles in Canada (N = 137). detail.abstract: Insider threats represent the most costly and least tractable class of security incident in the financial sector, where a single malicious insider event now averages several times more in losses than an external breach. Prevailing detection systems rely on opaque, machine-learned anomaly models that are difficult to audit, legally fragile under employment and financial-services regulation, and largely silent on the human and psychological dimensions of insider risk. This paper addresses that gap by introducing a fully deterministic, white-box behavioural risk-scoring framework that integrates multi-modal telemetry (authentication, removable-media, email, and file-access logs) with bounded psychometric signals derived from the Five-Factor personality model. The framework's central methodological contribution is an ethical-bounding mechanism: psychometric influence is mathematically capped below the alerting threshold, so personality data can amplify but never independently trigger a determination. Evaluated on the Carnegie Mellon CERT Insider Threat Dataset (r4.2; 1,000 users, 70 confirmed malicious actors), the framework achieves complete user-level recall (70/70; zero false negatives), functioning as a high-sensitivity screening layer whose precision-recall trade-off we characterise transparently, including an explicit analyst-triage cost model. Because every score is arithmetically reproducible, the system is auditable, evidentiary, and aligned with GLBA and SOX accountability requirements. We argue that transparency-not marginal predictive accuracy-is the decisive policy criterion for deployable insider-threat analytics, and we set out a governance-oriented research agenda for real-world validation.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence has arrived in human resource management faster than the evidence base, the governance practice, or the professional skill set needed to use it well. This article is written for the reader who must act before the research settles: the HR director choosing between vendors, the line executive asked to approve an automated screening tool, the scholar who wants a defensible map of where the practice actually stands. It does three things. First, it sets out a working taxonomy that separates three technologies too often discussed as one-predictive machine learning, generative language models, and agentic systems that act on their own outputs-and shows why the distinction changes what a manager should demand of each. Second, it reviews applications across the employee lifecycle, from workforce planning to offboarding, with an assessment of where the value is documented, where it is plausible but unproven, and where the claims outrun the evidence. Third, it offers a set of decision tools: a readiness diagnostic, a use-case prioritization matrix built on consequence and reversibility, decision rules for human oversight, a vendor due-diligence protocol, a measurement framework that distinguishes efficiency from effectiveness, and a staged implementation roadmap. The article closes with the regulatory landscape now binding on employers in the European Union and several United States jurisdictions, the implications for the HR function's own capabilities, and a research agenda for the questions practice is asking faster than scholarship is answering. The central argument is that the returns to AI in HRM depend far less on model sophistication than on three managerial choices: which decision the system is allowed to touch, what data it learns from, and who remains accountable for the outcome.

detail.abstract: Predictive-maintenance systems increasingly estimate equipment degradation and remaining useful life, while production Digital Twins support scheduling, flow analysis and virtual commissioning. These capabilities are commonly separated, and computer-vision (CV) observations are often treated as stand-alone inspection outputs rather than as state variables that modify maintenance and production reasoning. This paper proposes the Coupled Asset-Flow Cognitive Digital Twin (CAF-CDT), a multimodal methodology that synchronises three observation domains: machine/asset telemetry, visual observations from RGB, RGB-D, thermal and machine-vision cameras, and system/production data from PLC/SCADA, MES, WMS and ERP sources. The framework introduces a versioned multimodal Twin State containing equipment health, availability, capacity, visual condition, quality state, inventory, work-in-progress, order state and calibrated uncertainty. Sensor-derived degradation and CV-derived quality or physical-condition evidence are fused at twin level and propagated through a dynamic production graph along two coupled pathways: failure/availability impact and quality/rework impact. The resulting scenarios quantify throughput, WIP, starvation, scrap/rework, inventory and order-delay exposure before maintenance or production actions are selected. A knowledge-graph-supported cognitive layer assembles source provenance, dependencies, constraints and counterfactual outcomes into traceable recommendations. The methodology also specifies spatial and temporal registration of visual observations, CV uncertainty, edge-cloud deployment, multimodal ablation and staged validation using prognostics benchmarks, industrial vision datasets, simulation and eventual plant pilots. No empirical superiority is claimed prior to implementation.

detail.abstract: Robust inventory rules provide decisions under incomplete distributional knowledge and bounds on their performance. This paper evaluates these two roles jointly for selected newsvendor implementations in cost and profit forms, using common samples and explicit specification choices. A decision-equivalent distribution recovered from each monotone order path, an implied-service-level identity, and a sufficient condition for form invariance organize the comparison. In the reported backorder experiments, the Wasserstein-1 implementation reproduces the empirical-quantile decision; a calibrated Kullback-Leibler implementation has a non-monotone performance gap as sample size grows at high service levels; and a support box built from sample extremes deteriorates on unbounded demand. A zero-floored moment formula improves on the empirical rule in some small-sample settings, but is distinguished from the exact nonnegative-demand minimax solution. Specification sensitivity depends on the construction and the perturbation menu. The certificate analysis separates distribution containment, expected-performance coverage, and support-endpoint estimation. An endpoint impossibility result identifies a limitation of support-based claims, without implying that decision-changing distributionally robust guarantees are generally untestable. A classical order-statistic law quantifies plug-in chance-constraint miscalibration and supplies an explicit tolerance correction. Together, the findings provide a diagnostic procedure for evaluating an implementation's decisions, assumptions, and certificates separately.

detail.abstract: This note analyzes how alternative expectations about rival lending affect credit-supply dynamics in a Cournot-type oligopolistic banking market, where expected rival lending affects expected loan rates. Rational expectations yield the static Cournot-Nash equilibrium, whereas static and adaptive expectations generate first-order dynamics. A trend-based expectation rule introduces second-order dynamics: trend-extrapolative expectations tighten stability conditions, whereas trendreversal expectations can generate cyclical credit-supply movements. We show that trend-reversal expectations arise from local mean reversion toward a two-period reference level. The analysis identifies the parameter region in which local mean reversion generates cyclical credit-supply dynamics through complex roots. This provides an expectation-based mechanism for cyclical creditsupply fluctuations under Cournot-type lending competition, without depending on borrower-side amplification, default risk, or bank-capital constraints.

title: Agroecological Conditions, Dietary Diversity, and Childhood Stunting in Bangladesh: Evidence from a Control Function Approach
affiliations: University of New Mexico and University of New Mexico - Department of Economics

detail.title: Agroecological Conditions, Dietary Diversity, and Childhood Stunting in Bangladesh: Evidence from a Control Function Approach
detail.abstract: Childhood stunting remains a major public health challenge in Bangladesh, despite important progress in reducing undernutrition. While dietary diversity is widely recognized as essential for child nutrition, the causal effect remains unclear due to potential endogeneity between feeding practices and nutritional outcomes. This study exploits geographic variation in agroecological conditions across Bangladesh to estimate the causal effect of dietary diversity on stunting among children aged 6-23 months using nationally representative data from the 2022 Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey (n=1,228). We employ a Two-Stage Residual Inclusion (2SRI) approach, instrumenting dietary diversity with the aridity index to address unobserved confounding. The results indicate that an additional food group consumed is associated with a 25.1 percentage point reduction in stunting probability, while children meeting minimum dietary diversity (5+ food groups) are 47.6 percentage points less likely to be stunted. These effects remain consistent across alternative specifications using height-for-age z-scores and maternal empowerment proxies, and are robust to controls for household wealth, maternal education, and healthcare access. We document that maternal education and empowerment operate partly through dietary diversity, and that diet quality matters, as unhealthy food consumption negates diversity benefits. Our findings highlight the critical importance of improving dietary diversity during complementary feeding as a high-priority, evidence-based strategy for reducing childhood stunting. We recommend integrating targeted nutrition counseling into maternal and child health services, strengthening nutrition-sensitive agricultural systems in climate-vulnerable regions, and adopting multi-sectoral approaches that coordinate health, agriculture, education, and social protection efforts to enhance dietary diversity and nutritional outcomes.

detail.abstract:
Institutions govern through what they write down. Across four settings drawn from the author's deposited work, water and gas regulation in Virginia, Georgia and Tennessee, data-center zoning in Virginia counties, municipal finance in Radford and James City County, and the citations that generative search products display, this essay asks one question of each: who was assigned to ask how much. It sorts the failures it finds into three kinds. In the first, on the forms and orders read, the instrument has no field for the decisive fact, or has one the public cannot see: a water-delivery report with no line for the customer, a certificate whose every cost cell is redacted, a generation order that names no capacity factor. In the second, the fact was recorded and, on the records examined, nobody read it against anything. In the third, the fact was recorded, read, and said on the record by people with votes, and the institution wrote that down and proceeded. One thread in the corpus did something else with a gap. It built the missing series from federal filings written for another purpose, held that series against a second record, and then against its own earlier version. The essay treats that as the method. Every claim is page-referenced to one of twenty-two deposited works.

During the preparation of this work, the author used Claude (Anthropic) to locate and extract quotations and page references from the author's previously published papers, to check those quotations against the source files, and to refine the structure and language of the manuscript. After using this tool, the output was reviewed, edited, and verified by the author, who takes full responsibility for the content.

title: Port Environmental Performance and Greenhouse Gas Emissions: Efficiency Gains without Absolute Decarbonization
affiliations: Postgraduate Program in Environmental Science and Technology (PPGC&Tamb - UFMA),, Federal University of Maranhão, Federal University of Maranhão, Federal University of Maranhão and Federal University of Pernambuco (UFPE)

detail.title: Port Environmental Performance and Greenhouse Gas Emissions: Efficiency Gains without Absolute Decarbonization
detail.abstract: Ports are key nodes in global supply chains, yet growing activity can offset gains in environmental performance. This study examined whether institutional environmental improvements translate into greenhouse gas emission reductions at the Port of Itaqui, Brazil, using operational, hydroclimatic, and environmental data from 2012–2022. Exploratory machine learning and piecewise structural equation modeling showed that total emissions increased from approximately 190,000 to over 320,000 tCO₂e, while emission intensity declined, indicating relative efficiency gains. Machine learning models explained emissions better than the Environmental Performance Index, with cargo throughput emerging as the main predictor. Structural modeling confirmed a positive association between cargo throughput and emissions (β = 0.64; p = 0.032), whereas environmental performance was not significantly associated with emission reduction (β = −0.19; p = 0.660). These results indicate relative decoupling and show that port decarbonization requires absolute emission-reduction targets beyond compliance-based environmental metrics under sustained growth in port operations worldwide.

title: A targeted reanalysis of autosomal variants for egg production to 64 weeks in two White Leghorn lines identifies no robust association after multiple-testing correction

detail.title: A targeted reanalysis of autosomal variants for egg production to 64 weeks in two White Leghorn lines identifies no robust association after multiple-testing correction
detail.abstract: BackgroundEgg production to 64 weeks (EN64) is a commercially relevant trait in laying hens. We re-evaluated a targeted seven-gene autosomal variant panel for association with EN64 in two White Leghorn lines, ABWL and ASWL, previously examined for a three-gene subset using uncorrected permutation testing (Pal et al., 2023).MethodsThe analysis cohort comprised 87 hens (45 ABWL, 42 ASWL) with complete EN64 and line data. All 109 genotype-QC-passing biallelic autosomal SNPs (chromosomes 2, 4, 10, 24) were tested using pooled line-adjusted and within-line additive linear regression on continuous EN64, plus a secondary pooled line-adjusted High-versus-Low logistic analysis. Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction was applied within each model family.ResultsNo pooled autosomal SNP reached FDR significance for continuous EN64; the minimum P was 0.007199 at chr24:5,752,256 A>G (DRD2; FDR = 0.784669). Within-line leads were chr4:88,169,076 C>T in ABWL (P = 0.0203854, FDR = 0.745951) and chr24:5,748,172 T>C in ASWL (P = 0.019255, FDR = 0.545432); neither survived correction. No pooled High-versus-Low test was significant after correction; a nominal chr4:88,167,779 signal was excluded due to quasi-complete separation from sparse genotype counts.ConclusionsNo robust autosomal association with EN64 was identified in this 109-SNP panel. The chromosome-4, chromosome-2, and DRD2 patterns were nominal, line- or model-specific, and non-significant after FDR correction, and should be treated as hypothesis-generating, requiring independent validation and direct retesting of the variants previously reported significant for this panel (Pal et al., 2023).

title: Ideas and Firm Dynamics When It Takes Two to Tango

detail.abstract: Teams of inventors now produce over 80 percent of U.S. patents, up from just 45 percent in 1976. Over the same period, inventor employment has become increasingly concentrated in large firms, rising six times more than overall employment concentration. To explain these trends, we develop a new model of endogenous team formation within firms and embed it in a general equilibrium model of the inventor labor market. Teams increase firms' returns to scale by increasing the likelihood of productive matches between inventors. The value of these matches rises over time, possibly driven by increasing knowledge specialization. This causes large firms to expand and small firms to shrink in equilibrium, accounting for the observed increase in inventor employment concentration. Because firms do not internalize knowledge spillovers, there is misallocation of inventors across firms. The rise of team production amplifies this misallocation by a factor of six by reallocating inventors away from small firms that generate disproportionately large knowledge spillovers.

title: Class Discipline, Class Size and Scholastic Achievement Across Countries
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Class Discipline, Class Size and Scholastic Achievement Across Countries
detail.abstract: Formulating an education production function and using estimates of student and class discipline levels, this paper seeks to identify the relations between discipline, class size, teaching quality and scholastic outcomes. The data shows both individual and class-level discipline to be a powerful predictor of the PISA math score, while variance in discipline among classmates has a strongly negative effect. Furthermore, class discipline is correlated with larger classes. As a structural simulation demonstrates, the correlations observed in the data can be well explained by how schools allocate students and teachers to classes. This analysis allows for a break-down of the contribution of educational production factors and highlights the role of individual and class discipline to student achievements.

detail.title: Graying Asia: How Aging Is Reshaping Banking
detail.abstract: This paper explores how demographic shifts, particularly population aging, are reshaping banking in Asia-Pacific’s bank-dominated financial systems. Using household surveys as well as bank-level and country-level panel data, we show that aging populations are associated, with shifts in bank portfolios away from traditional loans (with lower loan-to-deposit and loan-to-asset ratios), driven by changes in households’ financial behavior. These changes affect banks’ funding structures, profitability, and risk profiles, with implications for financial stability. We also provide new evidence on cross-border dynamics, showing that demographic divergence spurs asset reallocation toward younger economies. Our findings highlight evolving risks and supervisory challenges as demographic transitions unfold unevenly across economies.

title:
Closing the Gap
A LIC's Policy Options under an Aid Shock
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title:
Closing the Gap
A LIC's Policy Options under an Aid Shock
detail.abstract: This paper uses a structural model calibrated to an aid-dependent economy to analytically explore the macroeconomic and distributional effects of a permanent aid cut under three alternative policy responses: non-concessional borrowing, domestic revenue mobilization, and uncompensated spending cuts. We find that a borrowing-only response leads to unsustainable debt and highly regressive outcomes. An uncompensated cut results in economic stagnation, higher poverty, and adverse inequality. Within the model, a strategy combining moderate borrowing with ambitious domestic revenue mobilization, while painful in the medium term, produces the most favorable path to fiscal sustainability and moderates the rise in poverty and inequality. These findings are analytical and model-based; they illustrate the trade-offs inherent in fiscal adjustment under aid dependence rather than prescribing specific policy actions.

title:
Pumps and Plates
Passthrough of International Fuel and Food Price Shocks to Domestic Markets

detail.title:
Pumps and Plates
Passthrough of International Fuel and Food Price Shocks to Domestic Markets
detail.abstract: Fuel and food constitute significant portions of consumer baskets, yet their prices are highly volatile. The renewed energy price shock in March 2026, driven by geopolitical disruptions and supply constraints, has highlighted the macroeconomic and distributional importance of how international price shocks transmit to domestic markets. Spikes in these prices can have major social, political, and economic implications. The conventional policy approach is to allow domestic retail prices to align with international prices while protecting the most vulnerable. However, many countries intervene in price settings to shield their domestic markets from global fluctuations. This paper provides a comprehensive assessment of the passthrough from global to domestic retail prices for four commodities: gasoline, diesel, wheat, and rice over the past two decades in many countries. We employ a dynamic model of local projections building on the work of Kpodar and Abdallah (2017). Our findings indicate that average passthrough is incomplete, with fuel exhibiting higher and faster passthrough than food. The extent of passthrough varies by period, region, and between commodity exporters and importers. We also examine asymmetric responses to global price shocks and find evidence of a ratchet effect: price increases are more likely to be passed through than decreases.

title: Tariff Pass-Through and Import Reallocation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Tariff Pass-Through and Import Reallocation
detail.abstract: We study how U.S. tariff hikes in 2025 have transmitted to import prices. Consistent with recent evidence, we find that duty-exclusive import prices at the variety (country-product) level do not adjust to tariffs, implying full pass-through to duty-inclusive prices at the border. At the product level, however, duty-exclusive aggregate import prices decline significantly with tariff increases. We show that this product-level decline is driven by within-product reallocation toward lower-priced sources—stronger in products facing larger tariff hikes—and operates primarily through the entry of lower-priced varieties and the exit of higher-priced ones. Estimates of variety appeal indicate that part of this reallocation reflects shifts toward lower-quality varieties, a channel that is also present in the 2018–19 U.S.–China tariff episode. These reallocation effects carry implications for consumer welfare and productivity through the quality of imported goods and inputs.

title: Taxing Cross-Border Services

detail.title: Taxing Cross-Border Services
detail.abstract: Faced with the limitations of existing tax frameworks for cross-border trade in services—particularly the lack of taxing rights over certain income from highly digital business models and the continuing scope for profit shifting through payments for cross-border services—countries and scholars have adopted or proposed a wide range of tax measures. This paper brings these measures together in a coherent framework and examines them from both an economic and a legal perspective. It documents how cross-border services trade has grown, become more digital in composition, and become increasingly concentrated across sectors, firms, and jurisdictions. It then develops a comparative synthesis covering destination-based consumption taxes such as VAT, gross-revenue taxes—notably digital services taxes—as well as income-based instruments such as nexus and withholding rules, and anti-avoidance rules aimed at limiting profit shifting through deductible cross-border payments. The paper argues that the economic incidence of each instrument is central to policy assessment and that evaluating these instruments in isolation obscures their interaction. Its main conclusion is that broader reliance on destination-based taxation can address many of the core problems raised by digitalized services trade more effectively than narrower, more distortionary alternatives.

title: Beyond the First Bond: Market Access and Debt Dynamics in Frontier Economics
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Beyond the First Bond: Market Access and Debt Dynamics in Frontier Economics
detail.abstract: We examine market entry and post-entry debt dynamics in Frontier Economies by grouping countries based on durability of market access using a two-step framework combining first Eurobond issuance with the reliance on private external creditors, validated through an unsupervised K-mean clustering. A discrete-time event LOGIT model finds that favorable global liquidity conditions and investor appetite open issuance windows for countries, but domestic pull factors—income, institutions, growth, and reserve buffers—ultimately determine success of market entry. Post-entry, Frontier Economies shift rapidly toward market borrowing, with looser fiscal stance as new financing source is unlocked. Along increased exposure to rollover and global financial cycle risks, debt decomposition exercise shows a worsening interest–growth differential and rising debt, driven mainly by primary deficits and higher interest burdens. Results underscore the need for credible medium-term fiscal frameworks, stronger debt management, and reserve buffers to manage the transition to market financing.

title: The Changing Landscape of Financial Integration in Asia-Pacific
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Changing Landscape of Financial Integration in Asia-Pacific
detail.abstract: Asia-Pacific has undergone a profound transformation over the past few decades, increasing its share in global trade and GDP. This paper assesses to what extent Asia-Pacific’s role in global finance has expanded commensurately and whether it has become more integrated by systematically analyzing crossborder financial data. We combine descriptive analyses of past trends in financial positions with network analysis to understand how inter- and intra- regional financial linkages have evolved for economies in the region. We find that Asia-Pacific’s role in global finance still significantly lags its role in global trade and that there is considerable heterogeneity within the region. Advanced economies in the region are well integrated into global financial markets, whereas most emerging markets exhibit more limited integration. Financial integration within the region is also low but diverges significantly by instrument. Intra-regional financial integration is advancing in foreign direct investment (FDI) and cross-border banking (the latter from low levels), but has remained limited in foreign portfolio investment (FPI). Gravity model analysis indicates a significant association between trade and FDI, but not between trade and FPI. We conclude the paper with policy recommendations to promote resilient financial integration in Asia-Pacific.

title: Industrial Policy and Trade Tensions in Strategic Sectors
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Industrial Policy and Trade Tensions in Strategic Sectors
detail.abstract: This paper examines the global trade and welfare effects of industrial subsidies, employing a multi-country, multi-sector general equilibrium trade model with economies of scale. We first estimate the magnitude of industrial subsidies across countries relying on a novel approach that exploits information on subsidy counts during the period 2015-23. We then quantify the impact of the implied subsidy rates on trade flows and find that subsidies boost net exports in strategic sectors especially for China, while causing export declines in competing economies. Subsidies by the EU and the US produce qualitatively similar but smaller effects, as these economies target relatively more non-strategic sectors. A decomposition of the trade effects highlights the role of economies of scale and productivity changes in explaining sectoral specialization in response to subsidies. Tariff actions in 2018-19 and since 2025 partly offset these trade patterns. While targeting strategic sectors, recent subsidies and import tariffs lower global welfare by creating distortions and negative cross-border externalities.

title: Settlement Risk and Currency Markets

detail.title: Settlement Risk and Currency Markets
detail.abstract: Settlement risk is a central friction in currency markets. We provide causal evidence on its pricing by exploiting Hungary's 2015 adoption of CLS, which introduced payment-versus-payment settlement, sharply reducing settlement risk. Using a difference-in-differences design, we find that currency excess returns decline by about ten basis points after CLS adoption, consistent with lower compensation for bearing settlement risk, while exchange rate volatility also falls. Deviations from triangular arbitrage conditions narrow, indicating a reduction in the effective cost of arbitrage and improved market efficiency. Additional evidence based on U.S.-specific holidays supports a mechanism operating through time-zone exposure. Our findings show that settlement risk is a priced friction and a source of limits to arbitrage in currency markets.

detail.abstract: Brand name changes (rebranding) are corporate strategies undertaken by companies in response to changes in business structure, strategic direction, market conditions, and regulatory environments. This study aims to analyze the motives behind companies' rebranding initiatives, identify the role of public policy in the brand transformation process, and examine its impact on product competitiveness. This study employs a descriptivequalitative approach through a literature review and analysis of several rebranding cases in Indonesia and internationally, including BreadTalk to Mako, Bank Niaga and Lippo Bank to CIMB Niaga, Gojek and Tokopedia to GoTo, Twitter to X, and Total to TotalEnergies. The analysis applies the perspectives of Brand Equity Theory, Brand Architecture, Brand Repositioning, and Corporate Brand Transformation. The findings indicate that rebranding is driven not only by marketing considerations but also by factors such as contract expiration, mergers, changes in corporate vision, intellectual property rights (IPR) protection, business competition, and regulatory requirements. Brand name changes can expand market relevance and strengthen competitiveness, but they may also create risks, including consumer confusion, brand equity erosion, resistance, and transition costs. Therefore, rebranding should be implemented through strategic planning, regulatory due diligence, transparent transition communication, and continuous performance evaluation.

title: The Generalized Jevons Paradox and the Future of Energy
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Generalized Jevons Paradox and the Future of Energy
detail.abstract: Global energy and materials are essential to the functioning of the economy and have significant implications for macroeconomics and the environment. At the same time, the world is not on track to meet Paris Agreement goals. This paper documents two stylized facts that connect these observations. First, the world economy is characterized by large embedded emissions and materials: different energies and materials are deeply entwined and interdependent. This has historically led to additive – rather than substitution – dynamics in energy and materials on a global scale. Second, historically there has been a strong positive correlation between efficiency in resource use and total resource use at a global scale. We synthesize these observations by introducing the Generalized Jevons Paradox (GJP). We argue that the GJP reflects the direct and indirect energy/material demand effects of long-term energy and material interdependencies, themselves shaped by market and geoeconomic power, trade arrangements, and financial factors. While future scenarios may diverge from historical data, including because of different population and growth trends, the GJP calls for caution in projecting energy and material flows within the energy transition framework, as it suggests that a declining share of fossil fuels in primary energy consumption can coexist with rising total fossil consumption, and thus rising global emissions – as observed since 2012. The GJP highlights the importance of policies to better allocate energy and material flows across sectors and countries and reduce supply chain vulnerabilities, but raises difficult distributional and political economy questions. Based on the GJP, the paper identifies three areas for research: the detailed analysis of the role of materials in supply chain vulnerabilities; the political economy of material flows; and multidimensional welfare analysis in decarbonization scenarios.

title: AI Intensity and Financial Market Responses to Economic Shocks: Evidence from US Industries
affiliations: Bank of England and Brunel University London - Department of Economics and Finance

detail.title: AI Intensity and Financial Market Responses to Economic Shocks: Evidence from US Industries
detail.abstract: This study investigates how the diffusion of Artificial Intelligence (AI) affects the transmission of macroeconomic shocks to asset prices. A new index of AI intensity for US industries is constructed by combining AI patents, the AI content of corporate disclosures, and the AI exposure of occupational mixes; this is then validated against survey evidence on AI. Panel local projection estimates indicate that AI-intensive industries earn significantly higher excess returns and command higher valuations in response to supply and technology shocks, but do not exhibit different responses to demand shocks. The response to the former type of shocks is economically large, robust across multiple independent supply-side identifications, and survives controlling for exposure to standard risk factors. It is driven by the industries that use AI rather than those that produce it, it is accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in valuations over the same horizon, and it is concentrated in high-volatility states. On the whole the results suggest that technological exposure is an important determinant of how aggregate shocks affect the cross-section of industries examined.

title: An Empirical Comparison of High-Dimensional Statistical Models vs. Machine Learning Models for Customer Churn Prediction

detail.title: An Empirical Comparison of High-Dimensional Statistical Models vs. Machine Learning Models for Customer Churn Prediction

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or non-financial interests relevant to this work.

detail.abstract: Customer churn prediction is a central task in marketing analytics, where datasets are frequently characterized by high dimensionality, class imbalance, and limited sample sizes. A substantial body of recent literature has favored ensemble machine learning methods such as XGBoost and LightGBM, yet the statistical modeling tradition continues to offer competitive and interpretable alternatives. Despite the coexistence of these two methodological streams, systematic head-tohead comparisons under controlled high-dimensional conditions remain scarce. This paper presents an empirical comparison of high-dimensional statistical models against state-of-the-art machine learning models for customer churn prediction. We evaluate a representative set of statistical approaches, including regularized logistic regression (Lasso, Ridge, and Elastic Net), linear and quadratic discriminant analysis, and partial least squares regression, against ensemble learning methods comprising Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and support vector machines. Experiments are conducted on multiple publicly available marketing churn datasets spanning telecommunications, banking, and subscriptionbased services. To simulate realistic high-dimensional regimes, we apply controlled feature expansion and noise injection, and we address class imbalance through stratified sampling, class weighting, and SMOTE-based augmentation. Models are assessed along four dimensions: predictive performance (AUC-ROC, F1-score, precision-recall AUC), robustness to increasing dimensionality and noise, computational scalability, and interpretability. Interpretability is quantified using feature importance stability across bootstrap resamples and SHAP-based attribution consistency. Our results indicate that while gradient boosting methods retain a modest predictive advantage in low-dimensional, large-sample settings, the performance gap narrows substantially-and in some cases reverses-as dimensionality increases and sample size decreases, where regularized statistical models exhibit superior stability and lower variance. We further find that statistical models consistently produce more stable feature attributions, suggesting a favorable trade-off between marginal accuracy loss and interpretability gain. These findings provide practical guidance for practitioners selecting churn models under highdimensional constraints, and they empirically substantiate the continued relevance of the statistical modeling paradigm. We conclude by outlining conditions under which each model family should be preferred and by identifying open challenges for hybrid statistical-machine learning approaches in marketing analytics.

title: Securities Lending as Wholesale Funding: Evidence from the U.S. Life Insurance Industry
affiliations: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

detail.title: Securities Lending as Wholesale Funding: Evidence from the U.S. Life Insurance Industry
detail.abstract: The existing literature assumes that securities lenders primarily respond to demand from securities borrowers and reinvest their cash collateral in short-term markets. We offer compelling evidence for a supply channel, using new data matching U.S. life insurers' individual bond lending and reinvestment decisions to the universe of securities lending transactions. We show that an insurer's decision to lend a bond is positively correlated with liquidity transformation in its lending program, even after controlling for demand for that bond. We discuss how using securities lending cash collateral as a source of wholesale funding might impair securities markets in times of stress.

title: AI Events, Persistence, and Volatility in US Utility and AI-Exposed Stocks: The AI-Power Channel
affiliations: Brunel University London - Department of Economics and Finance, University of Navarra - Department of Economics and University of Navarra - Pamplona Campus

detail.title: AI Events, Persistence, and Volatility in US Utility and AI-Exposed Stocks: The AI-Power Channel
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether four AI events between 2022 and 2025 - ChatGPT, GPT-4, the EU AI Act vote, and DeepSeek - changed the behaviour of fourteen US-listed stocks. The focus of the analysis is on two utilities that signed power purchase agreements with large AI companies, Constellation Energy and Vistra, which are compared with utilities that did not. The degree of persistence of the price of each stock is estimated in the periods around the events to establish whether it has changed. Volatility changes and whether the market reaction grows or fades across the events are also investigated. The results suggest that the events considered do not affect the degree of persistence of prices; however, they have an impact on their volatility for almost every stock. Among the utilities, only Constellation and Vistra exhibit a persistence shift that survives an adjustment for developments in the wider market, whilst utilities without power purchase agreements do not. Further, the response increases from one event to the next. A specific channel is identified: AI news moves a utility's price mainly when the firm has a contract to sell power to an AI company. However, this evidence is suggestive rather than conclusive.

detail.abstract: Rebranding is becoming increasingly important in the face of changing consumer preferences, technological advancements, shifts in business structures, and the dynamics of market competition. This paper aims to analyze rebranding as a strategy to enhance product competitiveness by integrating theories of marketing, regulation, consumer behavior, and market dynamics. The discussion employs a conceptual approach by examining the theories of brand equity, brand repositioning, brand architecture, crisis and reputation management, and cognitive fluency. The analysis is supported by case studies of rebranding in Indonesia and internationally, such as BreadTalk becoming MAKO, ACE Hardware becoming AZKO, Hoka Hoka Bento becoming HokBen, Gojek and Tokopedia becoming GoTo, as well as several global cases. The results of the analysis show that the success of rebranding is not determined solely by a change in name or visual identity, but by a company's ability to maintain brand equity, build new relevance, preserve consumer trust, comply with regulations, and create competitive value.

title: Local Trade Wars

detail.title: Local Trade Wars
detail.abstract: Modern protectionism has increasingly taken the form of decentralized trade coercion rather than multilateral escalation. What tariffs prevail in such local trade wars? How are welfare consequences shared between participants and bystanders? And can targeted economies credibly deter unilateralism? Using a multi-country, multi-sector Armington model that distinguishes the elasticity of substitution between domestic and imported goods from that across foreign varieties, we show that bilateral tariffs generate substantial third-market leakage. Applied to recent U.S. trade policy, this leakage magnifies U.S. losses and bystander gains under Trump 1.0, with bilateral Nash tariffs that are lower but more costly than those implied by standard models with a uniform trade elasticity. Trump 2.0's Liberation Day tariffs reverse these patterns by largely shutting down third-market leakage through broad-based tariff escalation. In a dynamic setting, no individual trading partner can credibly deter U.S. unilateralism: bilateral retaliation is either too weak or too costly. Only a near-universal coalition, broadly resembling the WTO membership, can flip U.S. incentives.

detail.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable source of behavioral responses for market research, but their choices can differ systematically from those of human respondents. Correction-based augmentation methods use a limited paired human-LLM sample to align these responses before downstream estimation; however, the learned correction faces finitesample uncertainty and is applied throughout a much larger auxiliary sample. We develop a Wasserstein-robust two-stage estimator that learns this correction over nearby plausible calibration distributions and applies it to auxiliary data for preference estimation under a common Fenchel-Young choice geometry. The framework generalizes the nominal two-stage estimator and develops a safe finite-dimensional formulation that jointly accounts for uncertainty in calibration inputs and human responses, including an exact convex conic representation for a class of linear correction models. Our finite-sample analysis establishes that robust calibration can provide a strictly stronger guarantee for the learned human-LLM relationship, with this improvement carrying through to downstream preference estimates. In a COVID-19 vaccine conjoint study, the approach improves parameter recovery and choice-probability fit relative to human-only estimation while reducing the human data required for comparable accuracy. A sports-car choice study extends the evidence to a multinomial setting. These findings show that human-anchored robust calibration enables LLM-generated responses to serve as a scalable and data-efficient complement for preference estimation.

detail.abstract: This article develops a conceptual and comparative analysis of continuous, cross-industry equipment modernization understood as an organizational capability rather than a discrete capital event. Drawing on a systemic modernization model organized as an iterative five-phase cycle, the study distinguishes two economic modes of industrial renewal-a product mode centered on one-time transactions and a capability mode centered on the durable transfer of problem-solving competence. Using a structured, criteria-based market-readiness framework, the article compares the conditions for adoption across three national contexts: the United States, Canada, and Ukraine. Drawing on official statistics, the analysis argues that the United States and Canada exhibit high-readiness conditions in which such a capability is adopted primarily through systematization of existing practices, whereas Ukraine represents a transitional context in which adoption is conditioned by uneven organizational readiness and would proceed through an initial educational and awareness-building stage. The article contributes a comparative framework for assessing how national industrial markets absorb capability-based, rather than product-based, modernization offerings, and identifies empirical questions for future testing.

detail.abstract: We provide the first occupation-level evidence on how the arrival of generative AI has been associated with labor demand in Japan. We construct a monthly panel of 58 mutually exclusive occupation units-55 detailed occupations plus the three major groups published without a detailed breakdown-from September 2021 to July 2026 using the Japanese government's official Employment Security Statistics (Shokugyo Antei Gyomu Tokei), which record new job openings registered at Hello Work public employment offices. We measure each occupation's exposure to generative AI using the "GPTs are GPTs" beta exposure score, mapped from U.S. SOC codes to Japanese occupation categories through a hand-built crosswalk. A continuous-exposure difference-indifferences design finds that job postings grew faster in more exposed occupations after the release of ChatGPT: the estimated post-period interaction is 0.276 log points per unit of exposure (SE 0.070, clustering at the major-group level), roughly 5 log points per standard deviation of exposure. The gradient, however, is identified only between broad occupational groups: pre-trends are rejected in the between-group design, the estimate collapses to zero when equal weights replace the detailcount weighting implicit in the panel, and a within-family specification with major-group-by-month fixed effects yields a precise null pre-trend but an uninformative post estimate (0.027, SE 0.26). We therefore interpret the results as descriptive evidence of a between-group exposure gradient that cannot be separated from correlated group-level shocks such as the post-COVID recovery-not as causal evidence that generative AI reshaped Japanese labor demand. We find no corresponding shift on the job-seeker side.

detail.abstract: Why do consumers remain committed to a generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) agent that currently underperforms available alternatives? Existing accounts of retention explain persistence primarily through satisfaction, switching costs, or investments already made. We argue that consumer-AI relationships require a prospective theory of commitment: consumers may invest in the anticipated future value of a specific human-AI dyad. We introduce Anticipatory Relationship Investment (ARI), defined as deliberate cognitive and behavioral effort to create future relationship-specific value with an adaptive AI agent. ARI includes reusable prompts, instruction sets, structured context, feedback routines, and memory-building intended to improve future interactions. The Anticipatory Investment Model explains how credible capability trajectories and trajectory-based bonding motivate ARI, which converts present effort into relationship-specific capital, can increase psychological ownership, buffers dissatisfaction, and makes benchmark-superior alternatives appear less attractive when they lack dyad-specific context. The model specifies three boundary conditions: trajectory credibility, asset portability, and task identity relevance. It distinguishes ARI from sunk cost, escalation of commitment, learning costs, switching costs, psychological ownership, personalization lock-in, technology optimism, and brand attachment through divergent predictions about future-return salience, emotional tone, and response to trajectory disconfirmation. The framework contributes to relationship marketing, switching-cost theory, and service-dominant logic by showing how 2 adaptive AI can convert consumer labor into prospective relationship capital, creating genuine value but also welfare risks when firms restrict transparency, portability, or exit.

detail.abstract: This study analyzes the transformation of BreadTalk into MAKO Cake & Bakery in Indonesia as a corporate rebranding process associated with the discontinuation of an international brand. The study aims to explain the mechanisms of brand equity transfer and their implications for consumer loyalty and the competitiveness of local brands. The analysis draws on Aaker's and Keller's brand equity perspectives, Muzellec and Lambkin's rebranding typology, as well as comparative cases of KFC, Twitter/X, and Dunkin'. The conceptual findings indicate that existing brand equity does not necessarily disappear but can be transferred and reconstructed through continuity in location, products, store experience, consumer trust, and brand associations. The concept of a stealth transition explains the gradual process through which consumers adopt the MAKO identity. From a competitiveness perspective, savings from licensing costs need to be balanced with investments in building brand equity. Rebranding also requires compliance with trademark regulations, consumer protection requirements, information transparency, halal certification and requirements, and hygiene standards. This study recommends managing the transition consistently and conducting longitudinal research to examine the transfer of consumer loyalty and retention as a foundation for sustainable local brand development in Indonesia.

detail.abstract: This study aims to deconstruct the phenomenon of "lying flat" (tang ping)-characterized by reduced labor output and consumption scaling back-occurring within modern, highly financialized urban systems from the perspectives of political economy, game theory, and human capital theory. A "low-desire life" is neither an idiosyncratic variation in individual preference nor a moral hazard; rather, it represents an individual's dominant strategy within a payoff matrix under multiple structural constraints, including "rate of return on capital far exceeding the rate of economic growth (r > g)," "credential inflation of human capital," and the "assetization of marriage and romance." However, the convergence of individual risk-aversion strategies generates aggregate negative externalities, leading to an absence of marginal buyers, shrinking tax bases, and actuarial imbalances in social security, which in turn drive the economy toward a balance sheet recession and a liquidity trap.

detail.abstract: Search is turning from a list of links into a written answer. This structured secondary review examines evidence published between January 2023 and September 2026 on how Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode, and answer engines such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Claude, change the way brands and publishers are found. More than twenty sources, from controlled experiments and behavioural panels to commercial datasets covering millions of keywords, are labelled by type and appraised for independence, transparency, scale, causal strength and ecological validity. Four findings emerge. Informational searches that show an AI answer generally earn fewer organic clicks, with most estimates of the drop between 35% and 61%, while branded searches can gain. Citation follows different rules from ranking: evidence-rich content raised visibility in generated answers by up to 40% in controlled tests, and only 38% of pages cited in AI Overviews in 2026 ranked in the top ten. Off-site brand signals correlate far more strongly with AI visibility than backlinks, although these are associations, not proven levers. AI assistants send well under 1% of website visits, yet retail data shows these visitors convert better than average. The paper contributes a search visibility chain, separate definitions of citation share, mention share and citation accuracy, four testable propositions, a click-risk scenario model, a query-exposure classification, an audit of thirteen GEO claims and a preregistration-style design for an Indian replication study. It offers a framework for measurement and testing and does not forecast traffic for any individual site.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the behaviour of condition-certification premiums during an asset boom-bust cycle using transaction data from the secondary market for collectible Pokémon trading cards between 2020 and 2026. Exploiting the exogenous demand shock triggered by COVID-19 lockdowns, liquidity expansions, and social media attention, we analyse price trajectories across an empirical 2×2 framework contrasting vintage (pre-2000) versus modern (pandemic-era) cards, and headline "grail" cards versus ordinary releases. We test whether professional authentication (PSA 10 Gem Mint certification vs. raw/ungraded copies) functions as a durable quality signal or an amplified vehicle for speculative premiums. The findings reveal a marked divergence: while vintage cards experienced classic bubble dynamics with iconic vintage assets appreciating over twenty-fold before collapsing, modern issues exhibited launch-scarcity decay or post-peak insulation. Crucially, proportional grading premiums (PSA 10-to-raw price ratios) were systematically higher for ordinary cards (mean ratio ≈ 114.4× vintage; ≈ 10.4× modern) than for hyped cards (mean ratio ≈ 36.9× vintage; 2.7× modern). This indicates that pervasive collector demand inflates baseline prices across all condition tiers for headline cards, compressing ratio premiums, whereas grading premiums in non-grail segments reflect extreme condition-scarcity compounded by low raw price denominators. These results demonstrate that third-party grading acts less as a uniform store of speculative value and more as an asymmetric, scarcity-dependent multiplier.

detail.abstract: Rebranding has become an increasingly important strategic decision for companies seeking to adapt their brand identities to changes in consumer preferences, market competition, technological developments, social expectations, and corporate strategic direction. This paper examines rebranding as a multidimensional process that extends beyond changes in brand names, logos, or visual identities. The study integrates perspectives from brand equity theory, brand architecture theory, market positioning and differentiation theory, corporate reputation and legitimacy theory, as well as public policy and legal regulation. The discussion focuses on the strategic motives behind brand-name changes, the regulatory factors that facilitate or restrict rebranding, and the implications of rebranding for product competitiveness. The analysis shows that rebranding can create opportunities for market expansion, repositioning, brand revitalization, improved brand recall, and the development of stronger relevance among new consumer segments. However, rebranding also creates risks, including the loss of existing brand equity, consumer confusion, weakened customer attachment, operational complexity, increased financial costs, and potential legal conflicts concerning trademark protection. From a legal perspective, rebranding must comply with corporate governance requirements, trademark regulations, consumer protection principles, and restrictions concerning public order, morality, and substantial similarity. Therefore, successful rebranding requires companies to balance continuity and change by preserving valuable elements of existing brand equity while developing a new identity that is relevant to future strategic objectives. The paper concludes that rebranding should be supported by a comprehensive brand-equity audit, early legal and intellectual-property assessment, integrated consumer communication, and systematic post-rebranding evaluation to maintain customer loyalty and strengthen long-term competitiveness.

detail.abstract: Rebranding has become an important strategy for companies in responding to the dynamics of the business environment, changes in ownership, restructuring, regulation, and shifting consumer preferences. This paper aims to analyze corporate rebranding in Indonesia from a marketing and strategic management perspective, to map its relationship with government policy, and to examine its implications for product competitiveness. The method used is a literature-based conceptual review covering rebranding, brand equity, brand architecture, the Resource-Based View, dynamic capabilities, regulation, and business competition. The findings show that rebranding can renew market relevance, strengthen positioning, increase innovation flexibility, and support efficiency through the reconfiguration of brand resources. However, identity change also carries the risk of eroding brand equity, creating confusion, reducing loyalty, and opening opportunities for consumers to switch to competitors. Regulation also influences the process through consolidation, brand protection, product licensing, and business-competition oversight. The success of rebranding depends on a company's ability to maintain value continuity, build a new identity, communicate the change consistently, and sustain competitiveness over the long term.

detail.abstract:
This paper proposes the establishment of the Nigerian Sectoral Training Consortium (NSTC): a multi-sector, industry-governed training framework comprising six Sector Training Guilds - covering Fintech and Technology, Manufacturing, Healthcare, Commercial Agriculture, Construction and Infrastructure, and Financial Services. Each Guild operates a two-track model: Track A for graduate and formal entry-level professionals, and Track B for the informal-to-formal credentialing of workers already operating outside the formal economy. The NSTC is funded through a reformed deployment of Industrial Training Fund (ITF) levy contributions, shared training infrastructure, and deferred trainee co-investment through Income Share Agreements.

The paper anchors this framework explicitly in ESG principles - mapping Guild activities to GRI 401, GRI 404, and GRI 413 under the Social pillar, and to the Governance pillar requirements of Nigeria's approaching 2028 mandatory IFRS sustainability reporting deadline. It argues that NSTC participation is not merely socially admirable but financially rational: generating auditable ESG metrics that improve participating companies' access to development finance, ESG-screened institutional investment, and capital market instruments.

Comparative analysis draws on five international precedents - Singapore's SkillsFuture initiative, South Korea's HRD Korea model, Rwanda's Priority Skills for Growth and Youth Empowerment Programme, South Africa's Sector Education and Training Authorities (SETAs), and Ghana's Council for Technical and Vocational Education and Training (COTVET) - identifying the design principles that distinguish successful models from cautionary tales, and adapting those lessons to Nigeria's specific institutional and political economy context. 

The paper closes with a phased 36-month implementation roadmap and targeted recommendations addressed to four institutional actors: industry associations, NGX-listed companies and major private sector employers, the Industrial Training Fund, and Nigeria's financial institutions and development finance partners.

detail.title: Social Sorting and Political Cleavages: Evidence from 2.5 Million Electoral Candidates
detail.abstract: How socially distinct are competing political parties' candidate pools? Since names encode cultural milieu, lineage, linguistic origin, and ancestry that standard socioeconomic variables miss, we measure social sorting across parties with names, predicting affiliation out of sample within municipality-years. Across more than 2.5 million local-election candidates, names pick the right-wing candidate in a random within-municipality pair 55.8% of the time in Spain and 56.5% in France. Given names alone do most of the work: around 55.0%. Under a stylized model of intergenerational transmission of political orientation, this translates to an implied gap of about 25 p.p. in parental naming propensities. The signal is stable in Spain but doubles in France by 2026. Within ideological families, names separate parties as sharply as across the right-left divide, even more so in France. The Spanish cleavage is linguistic and growing. The French one runs through names of immigrant origin and is strongest in large cities.

detail.title: From Departure to Development
detail.abstract: Emigration continues to shape the demographic and economic landscapes of Pacific Island Countries (PICs), though patterns and impacts vary widely across the region. This paper examines emigration trends in PICs and their implications on human capital and growth. We find that traditional emigration, which is largely characterized by a permanent relocation of young, highly skilled individuals—primarily to Australia and New Zealand—results in a brain drain in home countries. Moreover, many of these emigrants work in low-skilled jobs abroad, indicating significant skill mismatches and limited skill acquisition. More recent emigration has been driven by the expansion of labor mobility arrangements (LMAs) in Australia and New Zealand, involving low-skilled young workers who typically return home. These LMAs offer opportunities to mitigate brain drain, reduce youth unemployment, and support near-term economic growth through remittances. At the same time, children of LMA workers are more likely to drop out of school, thus undermining human capital accumulation and limiting long-term output gains. From a policy perspective, the results suggest that temporary labor mobility can be a helpful development instrument, while complementary policies are needed to safeguard children’s education, promote the productive use of remittances, and strengthen skills development and job creation at home.
